title: Friends murder youth after liquor party in Lucknow:Accused smashed victim's head with flower pot, throat slit; body burned to hide identity
summary: A young man in Lucknow was brutally murdered by his own friends after a dispute during a liquor party. The accused killed him, tried to destroy his identity by burning the body, and dumped it in an isolated area. Police have arrested two friends, while others are still absconding. Murder after liquor party The victim has been identified as Sachin Tiwari, a resident of Tikra village in Nagaram. Police said Sachin had gone to his friend Nihal Valmiki’s house for a liquor party on 7 January in the Sushant Golf City area of Lucknow. An argument broke out when the liquor and cigarettes ran out. During the fight, Sachin’s two friends attacked him. Attacked and killed The accused first hit Sachin on the head with a flowerpot. When he lost consciousness, they slit his throat with a knife, killing him on the spot. To hide the crime, the accused decided to burn the body. They wrapped Sachin’s body in a sheet, then tied it in plastic. Body taken on scooter After the murder, Nihal called his maternal cousin Karan Valmiki for help. The body was loaded onto a Honda Activa scooter and taken away. On the way, they found an empty field near Bhagirathi Enclave and dumped the body there. Body set on fire The accused tried to buy petrol in a bottle but were refused. Later, they bought petrol worth Rs 100 for the scooter. They returned to the spot, removed fuel from the scooter using the muffler, poured it on the body, and set it on fire. Sachin’s half-burnt body was later found lying in bushes. Mother and friend helped destroy evidence Police said Nihal’s mother was present in the house during the incident. She learned about the murder later and gave a sheet to cover the body. She, along with Karan, helped clean the house to destroy evidence. Nihal’s mother and another friend named Vinay are currently absconding. Police arrests and recovery Police arrested Nihal Valmiki and Karan Valmiki on Wednesday. A knife, the scooter, and two Android mobile phones were recovered. The name of a third accused has not yet been disclosed. What Sachin told his family Sachin’s brother Vipin said Sachin left home on 8 January, saying he was going to attend a court hearing with Nihal. Sachin had earlier been challaned for disturbing the peace. Clues from phone messages Before leaving, Sachin forgot his mobile phone at home. Later, he sent a voice message to his brother using Nihal’s Instagram account, saying he was going out and would return in two or three days. When he did not return even after three days, the family began searching for him. Post-mortem findings Sachin’s body was found on Friday near Bhagirathi Enclave. The post-mortem report confirmed death due to strangulation and throat injury. Police also revealed that six criminal cases were already registered against Sachin. Investigation continues Police said the investigation is ongoing. Efforts are being made to arrest the absconding accused and complete the probe.

title: Swami Rajrajeshwaram makes sharp comments on politics of country:Says power is not needed to save Sanatan dharma
summary: Sharda Peethadheeshwar Jagadguru Shankaracharya Swami Rajrajeshwaram Ji Maharaj arrived in Agra on Tuesday. During his arrival, he made sharp comments on the current politics and social situation of the country, saying that India was previously an agriculture-dominant country, but now has become a power-hungry country. Upon reaching Agra, Shankaracharya arrived at Jaipur House, Sumit Dhal's residence located near Ahimsa Park area of Agra Development Authority, where he was welcomed. Here, speaking about Sanatan Dharma, Shankaracharya said that there is no need for political power to protect Sanatan Dharma, because power itself bows down before dharma. Calls Sanatan as god's dharma He said that Sanatan Dharma is God's dharma and it does not need any political protection. India was previously an agriculture-dominant country, but now has become a chair (power) dominant country. On the question of making India a Hindu nation, he said, What does not exist is what needs to be created. It is not correct in terms of words to talk about creating something that already exists. However, he also clarified that while he respects this sentiment, he does not agree with the choice of words being used on this subject. Minorities majorites both greedy for power Commenting on politics, Shankaracharya said that whether minorities or majorities, both are greedy for power. For this reason, both engage in appeasement and practice politics of vote collection. He said that today many political parties are more inclined towards their political agendas than the interests of the public and nation. Comments on constitution Regarding the constitution, he said that those who have the right to change the constitution should make the changes. Those who raise the question of how the constitution will be changed should also be asked why they were elected and sent to parliament.

title: Raebareli BA student adopts ascetic life at Magh Mela:Ran away from Raebareli to reach Magh Mela; crying mother said - Babaji please return my son
summary: A 21-year-old BA student from Raebareli took sannyasa at the Magh Mela. He left home on January 1st, saying he was going to church. However, he reached the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. There he met a saint and renounced his worldly life. His family came to know about this after seeing his mobile status. After this, the family members reached Prayagraj and tried to convince their son. But he was not ready to return home. The mother cried and said to the saint - Give my son back. But the saint said that he now belongs to us. The father says that his son is the only hope of the house. The whole family's expectations were on him, but he chose to become a saint. The incident is from Maharajganj town. Navin Kamal (48) lives in Maharajganj town. He runs a photocopy shop in front of the tehsil. At home, there are his father, Mahavir (92), mother, Shankar Devi (90), wife Soni Rastogi (45), three daughters, Neha (26), Rani (21), Navya (13), and a son, Amar Kamal Rastogi (22). Son Amar is a second-year BA student at Firoz Gandhi Degree College. Along with studies, he used to run a Jan Seva Kendra (CSC) center below the Bank of Baroda branch. Amar's elder sister, Neha, has completed her studies. Second sister Rani is pursuing graduation. Third sister, Navya, is also studying. Father said - Found out through mobile status Father Naveen said - My son Amar told us on January 1st that he was going to church. He had a Christ tattoo on his hand, and he regularly went to church. That's why no one said anything. However, he didn't return home all night. The next day, when we called, we found out that he had gone to the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. After going there, he posted a status on mobile about living a life of renunciation. That's when we learned that he had taken sannyasa. Even after 4 days, when Amar didn't return home, my daughters talked to him on the phone, but he wasn't talking properly. The next day, we reached Prayagraj with the family and started searching for him. When we met Amar there, we saw that he had taken sannyasa. He was with a baba. We requested the baba many times to let Amar return home. But the baba replied that this son is now mine. He is in a life of renunciation and won't return. Even Amar's sisters tried hard to convince him to return home, but he was not ready. Father said - The whole family is in shock since his departure Amar's mother is in terrible condition, crying constantly due to his actions. Grandparents are all stunned by this incident. Amar is the only son of the family and has the responsibility of carrying forward family traditions. Amar was a good student and also ran a public service center, but now he has worn the Tulsi mala. He used to take complete care of his grandparents. Pleased with his service, his grandparents had transferred their house located in front of the Bank of Baroda in the town to Amar's name. Amar used to run the public service center in that house. Navin Kamal alleged that Uday, his uncle and elder father, was angry about the house being in Amar's name. They secretly tried to get Amar to meet with holy men and saints. He accused the brothers of trying to control his son's mind through occult practices. Mother Soni said - He was our only hope Amar's mother, Soni Rastogi, said tearfully - I have tried everything possible to bring my son back. He is my only son, who is the hope of our life as husband and wife. Since COVID, my husband's health has been poor. Because of this, my only son was handling the household responsibilities. We will make every effort to bring back our son. We will bring him home at any cost. Brothers play the most important role in their sisters' weddings. After all, who will play that role now? Who will perform those rituals? Neighbor Priyanshu said - Amar suddenly adopted an ascetic life, which has left everyone in shock. His behavior towards people was very good, which is why people liked him. During the operation of the Jan Seva Kendra, work that would take about two to two and a half hours in the bank, Amar would complete in half an hour. His Jan Seva Kendra had more crowds than the bank. There is an appeal to Baba to send this naive child back home from his place. So that harmony and peace remain among his family members. The neighbor said that the boy may have taken this step under the influence.

title: Dog performs parikrama of idols for hours stretch in Bijnor:Locals call it miracle while veterinarians term it mental issue
summary: A surprising incident has come to light from UP’s Bijnor district, where a dog has been continuously circling the idols of Lord Hanuman (Bajrangbali) and Maa Durga inside a temple for the past three days. The sight has left locals astonished, as the dog has been performing the ritual-like parikrama for several hours at a stretch. Circling near idols without food or water According to eyewitnesses, the dog circled Lord Hanuman’s idol for the first two days. On Wednesday, it began circling the idol of Maa Durga. The dog has reportedly continued without eating or drinking. When tired, it is seen lifting one leg while walking. See 3 photos related to the incident... Crowd gathers, miracle claims arise Notably, the incident took place at an ancient Hanuman temple in Nandpur village of the Nagina area. Devotees and onlookers have gathered in large numbers. Some are calling it a miracle, while others believe the dog is a devotee. Videos of the incident have gone viral on social media. Dog reached temple suddenly Villagers said the dog was first seen circling the Hanuman idol early Monday morning. It showed no fear and did not stop. On Wednesday, after circling Hanuman again, the dog briefly left and returned within 15 minutes to start circling Maa Durga’s idol. Veterinary team checks dog A veterinary team examined the dog and left after finding no immediate health concerns. The dog continues to circle the idols without consuming food. Similar incident in Mainpuri A comparable incident was reported earlier this month at the Kal Bhairav temple in Mainpuri, where a dog was seen continuously circling a banyan tree near the temple without eating or drinking. What do veterinarians say? Veterinarian Dr PN Singh said the incident should not be termed a miracle. He explained that dogs can sometimes develop behavioural or mental issues, leading to repetitive, obsessive actions.

title: Police stop Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad in Ghaziabad:Convoy detained for 30 minutes amid tension, linked to Sonu Kashyap murder case
summary: Police stopped Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad at UP Gate in Ghaziabad. They did not allow his convoy vehicles to proceed further. During this time, he also argued with Kaushambi SHO Ajay Sharma and Indirapuram ACP Abhishek Srivastava. The ACP said - It's orders from senior officials, you cannot go to Meerut. For about 30 minutes, the Ghaziabad police have stopped the minister's convoy vehicle. There are 3 vehicles in Sanjay Nishad's convoy. He was going to Meerut to meet Sonu Kashyap's family. 3 days ago, Ghaziabad police had also tried to stop Nagina MP Chandrashekhar in Ghaziabad. But he had reached Kashi Toll in Meerut's border by taking a 60-kilometer detour. ACP Abhishek Srivastava said, Minister Sanjay Nishad has agreed to return. However, he is still waiting there. Some vehicles from his convoy are also present. Meerut SP Traffic Raghavendra Mishra is also at the spot. Minister Sanjay Nishad will leave for Delhi after completing all formalities. Meanwhile, before going to Meerut, Minister Sanjay Nishad had said - We are going to Meerut to get justice for Sonu Kashyap. We will meet his mother and family, support them, and talk to the local officials. I will also meet CM Yogi regarding the investigation. On January 8, the partially burnt body of a young man, Sonu Kashyap, was found in Sardhana, Meerut. According to the police, the youth was first killed by being hit with bricks. After that, the body was burnt with mobile oil to destroy evidence. However, people say that Sonu Kashyap was burnt alive. The accused are from the Thakur community. On January 12, SP MLA Atul Pradhan from Sardhana met the victim's family and provided financial assistance of 1 lakh rupees. Regarding this case, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati, and Chandrashekhar all posted on X. Congress also expressed displeasure. Along with this, Chandrashekhar posted again on X, writing that I will come to meet the victim's family soon. Jwalagadh is adjacent to Kapsad village Jwalagadh village is adjacent to Kapsad village of Thakur Chaubisi in Sardhana. Kapsad is the same village where, on January 8, a youth from the Thakur community murdered a Dalit woman, Sarita, and then kidnapped her daughter, Ruby. After this, the matter took the form of caste politics. An unofficial curfew was imposed in Kapsad village. The opposition created an uproar due to the girl not being recovered and the accused not being arrested. Many leaders made posts. They also visited the family. The situation became so tense that the police turned the entire village into a cantonment. After 60 hours of kidnapping, police arrested the accused and safely recovered victim, Ruby. Now, due to a Thakur versus OBC case in the neighboring village, politics has started again. In this case, too, the accused is a Thakur, while the deceased is OBC. Protests from Meerut to Lucknow On January 13, protests were held in this matter from Muzaffarnagar, Meerut, to Lucknow. SP workers were dragged. Chandrashekhar was prevented from meeting the victim's family in Muzaffarnagar. On January 12, the victim's family protested at the DM office in Muzaffarnagar and demanded justice. Meanwhile, on January 13, when some SP leaders went to meet the victim's family in Jwalagadh in Meerut to express condolences, the police stopped them from meeting. There was quite a commotion there.

title: Doctor’s throat slit by Chinese kite string, dies in agony:Bike ride turns fatal in Jaunpur; sharp string cuts neck bone during festival day
summary: A doctor died in Jaunpur after his throat was cut by a Chinese kite string. He was returning home on his bike. On the way, the Chinese string got caught in his neck and kept cutting through. The string was so sharp that it cut through to his neck bone. He fell face down. Blood started gushing from his neck. The road was covered in blood. The suffering doctor could neither move nor remove his helmet. People nearby immediately called an ambulance and took him to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The accident occurred around 12:30 PM on Wednesday at Prasad intersection in Line Bazar police station area. The deceased was identified as Dr. Sameer Hashmi (28), a resident of Kerakat. Police reached the spot upon receiving information. The body was sent for post-mortem. See images related to the incident... Among 4 brothers, Samir was the youngest, eldest brother works in Saudi Arabia Dr. Samir Hashmi was fourth among Mukim's 4 sons from Kerakat. The eldest brother Shahid works in Saudi Arabia. Golu is second and the third brother's name is Javed. Golu is an AC mechanic in Mumbai, while Javed looks after the band party business with his father. Father Mukim said - Samir was a doctor. He studied from Uttarakhand. He has a clinic in Kerakat. He was both a medicine department doctor as well as an orthopedic doctor. Father said - Tried to stop him a lot but he didn't listen Father said - This morning he left home on his bike saying he was going to meet some doctor. I stopped him saying today is a festival. Don't go anywhere, but he didn't listen. Mother said crying - Son had gone to clinic Mother Bano Khatun who reached the hospital said - Son Sameer had left saying he was going to the clinic. Shortly after, we got news of the accident. When I reached here, I found my son's dead body. Chinese kite string has become deadly in UP in recent days.... News is being updated continuously...

title: Fire breaks out for second day at Prayagraj Magh Mela:Over 20 tents affected; cause of fire yet to be ascertained
summary: A major fire broke out at the Swami Ram Sewak camp of the Prayagraj Magh Mela on Wednesday evening, triggering panic in the area. Thick smoke and towering flames were visible from nearly five kilometres away. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained. The blaze erupted in Sector 4, along the Lower Marg, and quickly spread to more than 20 camps. Fire brigade teams rushed to the spot and began spraying water to control the flames. The entire area was sealed to prevent the fire from spreading further, while police personnel and saints present at the mela initiated rescue operations. At present, 10 fire tenders and 10 ambulances are deployed at the site. Around 30 fire department personnel are engaged in shifting people to safer locations. There is no immediate information on the extent of damage or casualties, and the exact cause of the fire remains unknown. Notably, a similar incident occurred just 24 hours earlier at the Narayan Shukla Dham camp on Tuesday evening. In that fire, 15 tents and 20 shops were gutted, and one Kalpavasi sustained burn injuries. The incident had taken place in Sector 5 of the Magh Mela area. Five fire tenders were pressed into service at that time, and after nearly one and a half hours of effort, the fire was brought under control. The cause of that fire was reportedly a short circuit. Entire Narayan Dham camp destroyed The Narayan Dham camp had 15 tents housing over 50 Kalpavasis. As the fire spread, thick smoke engulfed the camp, leading to chaos as people rushed out to save themselves. Police personnel stationed there alerted the fire department, and within 10 minutes, fire tenders began arriving one after another. By the time the fire was doused, the main Narayan Dham camp had been completely reduced to ashes, with all tents destroyed. Kalpavasis were safely evacuated, but around 20 nearby shops were also burnt. Satua Baba, a close associate of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, reached the spot and took stock of the situation from officials. The tents at the camp had reportedly been set up by Lallu and Sons and Lallu Brothers, companies belonging to the same family. Firefighters continued spraying water to ensure the flames were fully extinguished, while rescue and relief operations remained underway.

title: UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary says SIR is government's responsibility:Vows to support process ensure no eligible voter is excluded
summary: A fresh political and administrative debate has emerged in UP over responsibility for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. While CM Yogi has indirectly placed the onus on BJP organisation workers for the alleged reduction of nearly four crore voters during the SIR process, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary has now stated that SIR is the responsibility of the government. Party to support process but not take accountability According to Chaudhary, the party organisation is fully prepared to extend cooperation, but the execution and accountability of the SIR process rest with the government. Pankaj Chaudhary made these remarks during a meeting of BJP regional presidents held at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow on Tuesday, January 13. Indication of growing friction between state government BJP organisation Coming shortly after he meets with Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Delhi, Chaudhary’s statement is being interpreted in political and administrative circles as an indication of growing friction between the state government and the BJP organisation over roles, coordination and accountability. During the meeting, the BJP state president said, SIR is the government’s responsibility. Our role is to cooperate fully so that not a single eligible voter is left out of the electoral rolls. Why Chaudhary took a clear stand Shadow of 2024 Lok Sabha elections The BJP’s experience in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections has played a major role in shaping the current debate. During those elections, thousands of voters across multiple constituencies discovered that their names were marked as “deleted” in the voter lists provided to polling officials, even though their names appeared in voter lists held by the party and its candidates. This discrepancy was widely considered a key factor behind the BJP’s electoral setbacks in several seats. Political experts believe that to avoid a repeat of such a situation, Pankaj Chaudhary has deliberately clarified that SIR is an administrative exercise and not the responsibility of the party organisation. What CM Yogi Adityanath said on SIR On December 14, 2025, during a BJP event at Ram Manohar Lohia University in Ashiana, Lucknow, organised ahead of the party’s state president election, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath delivered a pointed message to party workers. Referring to the 2027 Assembly elections, Yogi said the opposition lacked strength but warned against complacency. He remarked that excessive generosity and blind trust sometimes lead to self-inflicted setbacks. Addressing the SIR process directly, the CM said the Election Commission was conducting SIR across the state, but claims of 98 to 100 percent completion at the local level were not accurate. He described SIR as an opportunity to purify the voter list and resolve complaints that surface during elections. Highlighting a significant numerical gap, Yogi said UP has a population of around 25 crore, of which 64-65 percent should be above 18 years of age. On this basis, the voter list should contain approximately 16 crore names. However, he pointed out that while the January 2025 voter list had 15.44 crore voters, the SIR process had reduced the number to around 12 crore, leaving a gap of nearly four crore voters. CM said, These missing voters are not opposition supporters. Around 85 to 90 percent of them are our voters. Chaudhary’s broader political strategy CM raised issue before national leadership

title: Parts of Manikarnika Ghat demolished in Kashi:Locals protest for removal of Ahilyabai statues; DM says all findings during excavation to be preserved
summary: Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi is being demolished as part of a redevelopment project, and a new ghat will be constructed at the site. The design for the new structure has already been finalised. Manikarnika Ghat was originally built in 1771 by Lokmata Devi Ahilyabai Holkar and was later renovated by her in 1791. Protests erupted recently after her statue was found amid the debris during demolition work. The foundation stone for the project was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2023. However, construction remained stalled for nearly one-and-a-half years due to flooding in the Ganga. Work has now resumed at a faster pace to complete the project. The redevelopment plan includes renovation of both Manikarnika Ghat and Harishchandra Ghat. Read why there are protests... Included in 84 major ghats Manikarnika Ghat is among the 84 main ghats of Kashi. It is one of the five ghats built by Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. According to mythological beliefs, Lord Vishnu's jewel fell at this place, which is why it was named Manikarnika. The ghat combines traditional architecture, historical sculpture and religious faith. Devi Ahilyabai had developed many facilities here for pilgrims. Now the redevelopment work of Manikarnika Mahashamshan Ghat is underway. The executing agency has started construction work on the ghat. Meanwhile, with the help of hydra, the stones of the permanent ghat are being broken and loaded into tracks to be sent across the Ganges with the help of large boats. However, during this operation, some people alleged that the 300-year-old Mani (stone structure) present there has also been removed. Some people present there registered objections to this, but the administration pacified them through explanation and understanding. Upon receiving information about the protest, DCP, ACP, ADCP and ADM City had reached the spot. What people say? Sanjay Mishra said, "Our family has been taking care of this Mani (sacred stone/idol). But the administration demolished it without any notice. He said that it had a statue of Ahilyabai Holkar and also a Shivling. Today we all gathered here and have one demand from our administration that our Mani should be returned to us again.' Mayank Pal said - We all are from Pal community, the statue that was broken here should be re-installed. Otherwise, we will launch a big protest. Today we were all gathering here, but the police administration removed us. There was an ancient statue here which has been broken, but no one is ready to accept it. Now first know what is the project The redevelopment work of Manikarnika is to be done with CSR funds at a cost of Rs 18 crore. The executing agency is being formed under the supervision of the Municipal Corporation. The construction here will now be done according to G plus one. According to the officials of the executing agency, work is to be carried out in an area of 29350 square meters. The soil here is marshy, so piling has been done up to 15 to 20 meters deep. Piling work has been done up to hard soil. So that the construction here does not face any problems during floods. Now know how the ghat will look A 25-meter high chimney will also be installed at this crematorium so that the ashes from the pyre rise into the air and don't enter homes. The renovation will include sacred water tanks for bathing the dead bodies, waste trolleys, and tonsure areas. The covered cremation area will have five berths, service area, waste collection system, stairs, waiting area, ground floor registration room, 18 platforms for open cremation, wood storage area, community waiting room, and construction of two community toilets. The entire construction work here will be done using stones from Chunar and Jaipur. Both major crematoriums have become ruins, work has now gained pace The renovation of these two ghats began 19 months ago. A plan worth crores was made to provide additional facilities here. A plan was prepared to develop these two ghats through CSR funds. The work also began. PM Modi laid the foundation stone for this work in 2023. Not only this, the work remained stopped for about one and a half years due to floods. But now speed has been brought to complete this plan. The statues and artifacts found from Manikarnika Ghat will be preserved. These include the statue of Rani Ahilyabai as well. What DM says... DM Satyendra Kumar said that millions of people come to Manikarnika Ghat every year for last rites. There is a lack of space and difficulty in maintaining cleanliness arrangements. Projects have been developed keeping those problems in mind. He said that some videos are also being created and released on social media using AI. But the idols that were in the Mani there have been preserved in collaboration with the Sanskrit department and when the construction work is completed, those idols will also be installed at the same place. Original manikarnika Ghat will not be harmed anyway He also said that the original temples at Manikarnika Ghat will not be harmed in any way, the temples will remain as they are. The artworks that are being talked about being damaged have been preserved and no attention should be paid to any kind of rumors. He said that those who are spreading confusion about this are being identified and action will be taken against them if needed.

title: Namo Shakti Rath to hold breast cancer screening in Varanasi:Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma flags off 20 chariots, 7.5 lakh women to be screened
summary: Inspired by the Prime Minister, Namo Shakti Rath was launched on Wednesday from the Commissioner's Hall for timely detection and prevention of breast cancer in women. This initiative is inspired by the Prime Minister's vision of Healthy Women-Empowered Family. This scheme is an important step towards strengthening women-centric preventive healthcare services. Present during this occasion were Rajya Sabha MP Dr. Kartikeya Sharma, Commissioner S Rajalingam, District Panchayat President Poonam Maurya, and DM Satyendra Kumar who flagged off 20 Namo Shakti Raths. These vehicles will conduct free breast cancer screening for women aged 18 years. Of these, 9 vans will operate in rural areas and 11 in urban areas. Chief Development Officer Prakhar Kumar Singh and Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rajesh Prasad were also present during this event. See three pictures related to Namo Shakti Rath launch... Screening will be done in Varanasi district with 20 vans In the program, Rajya Sabha MP Dr. Kartikeya Sharma said - Prime Minister launched the Namo Shakti Rath in Haryana on his birthday September 17, 2025. After this, today this rath is going to run in Varanasi. There are 20 vans through which screening will be conducted in urban and rural areas. AI will be used All these vans are modern and equipped with AI technology. This work has been started with the Prime Minister's inspiration to bring this system and facility to doorsteps using no-touch, non-invasive, no-radiation technology. There are 7.5 lakh women in Varanasi district and we have to complete this. He said the treatment for this problem is to detect it early. Machine will detect body changes without pain During this time, Commissioner S Rajalingam said - Half the population consists of women. Currently, there have been changes in lifestyle which are causing people to be affected by diseases like cancer. The Namo Shakti Rath is equipped with technology for breast cancer screening that can identify early vascular changes in the body without any pain or contact. Therefore, we appeal to all of you to bring women from your homes along with more people for screening to get information about this disease. Screening will also be done in rural areas Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rajesh Prasad said - Currently, about 9 lakh people die from cancer. Of these, a very high number of patients have breast cancer. Therefore, breast cancer screening is extremely necessary for women above 18 years of age. He informed that 20 Namo Shakti Raths (vans) have been provided for Varanasi by the ITV Foundation. Of these, 9 vans will operate in rural areas and 11 vans will run in urban areas. ASHA and Anganwadi workers will cooperate The Chief Medical Officer said - Today ASHA and Anganwadi workers were called in this program. They have been explained the working of this machine. With the cooperation of ASHA and Anganwadi workers, women will be motivated for screening by giving prior information. Its purpose is to make health services accessible at the community level through modern technology.

title: Road accident victim’s family to receive ₹17.29 lakh compensation:Agra court orders UP Roadways to pay compensation; accident caused by bus driver’s negligence
summary: The family of the carpet artisan who lost his life in a road accident with a UP Roadways bus has now received justice. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) has ordered that UP Roadways will pay Rs 17 lakh 29 thousand to the deceased's family, along with 7 percent annual interest. Accident occurred due to negligent bus driving The case is related to 42-year-old Jagdish, a resident of Shivpuri village in Fatehpur Sikri police station area. Jagdish was a carpet artisan and was returning home via Kirawali on his motorcycle around 8:30 AM on October 20, 2020. On the Kirawali highway near Reela Yans petrol pump, Mathura depot's Roadways bus driver Satyabhan Singh, driving fast and negligently, collided with Jagdish's bike. The accident was so severe that Jagdish died on the spot. Family knocked on door for justice After the accident, Jagdish's family filed a petition in the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal for compensation. While hearing the case, the tribunal judge Narendra Kumar Pandey accepted the evidence and arguments of advocate Anil Kumar. Interest will be given from the petition date. The tribunal said in its order that UP Roadways will pay a total of Rs 17.29 lakh, along with 7 percent annual interest from the date of filing the petition to the deceased's family. Big relief for the family. This decision will provide financial support to the deceased Jagdish's family. Also, this decision is being considered as a strict message for careless vehicle drivers that they will have to pay the price for negligence on the road.

title: 'Nobody buying tooth-twigs at Magh Mela, fake videos being made':Vendors claim 'datun' not even being taken for free; what's the truth?
summary: Prayagraj’s Magh Mela has recently seen widespread discussion around the business of selling neem twigs (datun), after several social media videos claimed vendors were earning more than ₹1,000 a day and even lakhs during the fair. Influenced by these claims, many people traveled to the Mela hoping to make quick money by selling datun. However, ground reality tells a different story. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to several vendors at the fair to verify these claims and found that sales remain extremely low, with many sellers unable to recover even basic costs. Read the full report.. Footfall picks up, but datun sales remain weak The Magh Mela began on January 3. Due to cold weather, attendance was low during the first week, but over the past five days, a steady stream of devotees has been arriving daily for holy dips. Around 3,000 small and large stalls have been set up across the fairgrounds. Alongside regular sellers of garlands, prasad, and water cans, many vendors have added neem twigs to their stalls after watching viral videos suggesting high profits. Several newcomers also arrived specifically to sell datun. Despite increased footfall, most vendors report negligible demand for neem twigs. 'Hardly any sales,' say local vendors Sanju Devi, a vendor from Gopiganj, about 62 km from Sangam, usually sells water containers and prasad near the ghats. This year, she also stocked neem twigs. She said, The twigs are just drying up. Some days maybe one or two sell, but that doesn’t help. People even ask for 10 twigs for ₹5. Sometimes we tell them to just take them. Sanju added that she does not use a mobile phone but heard from others that videos showing big profits were circulating, which encouraged many people to come and sell datun. Fifteen-year-old Sarita, who came to the fair for the first time, also brought neem twigs after watching similar videos. She added, It’s been 10 days and not even one twig has sold. We thought we would earn well, but nothing like that is happening. Less than ₹100 in sales in 10 days Rajendra, who came from Mirzapur, was found resting near his stall with a bundle of datun lying unsold. He said he has been selling since January 3 but has not managed to sell even ₹100 worth of twigs. He said, People don’t even stop to ask. Maybe most visitors bring their toothbrush and toothpaste from home. Another nearby vendor, Sangeeta, blamed misleading social media content. He also said, Many people are making fake videos. They come only to shoot videos and then leave. They claim earnings of ₹50,000 to ₹1 lakh, but sellers here are barely making anything. Over 200 vendors left after failing to sell Premchand Nishad from Bhadohi arrived with multiple sacks of neem twigs. He said sales have been extremely poor this year. He said, People came from 300–400 km away hoping to earn, but many left after seeing there was no demand. More than 200 boys who came with us have already returned. Premchand believes fewer visitors are buying datun due to safety concerns after last year’s incidents, and because most pilgrims bring personal hygiene items with them. He expressed frustration toward video creators. Nishad added, People trusted those videos and brought large stocks. Now they are stuck here with no buyers. It’s embarrassing to even talk about how little we sold. Role of ‘Datun Boy’ and viral videos Akash Yadav, popularly known as the 'Datun Boy', gained fame during the previous Mahakumbh after claiming he earned over ₹1 lakh by selling neem twigs. He was later invited to appear on a television show. Akash, originally from Jaunpur, returned to the Magh Mela this year along with 30–40 others. Several videos were recorded showing datun sales and claiming daily earnings of ₹1,000–₹2,000. These clips circulated widely on social media and encouraged many newcomers to try the business. However, multiple vendors and on-ground verification indicate that many of these videos were scripted and did not reflect real sales conditions. Why demand remains low According to vendors, the primary reason for poor sales is that most pilgrims now carry toothbrushes and toothpaste from home. Those staying in camps or lodges also bring their own supplies, reducing the need for traditional datun. Additionally, competition has increased sharply, with many sellers offering the same product, further lowering individual sales. Ground reality contradicts online claims Dainik Bhaskar’s field reporting confirms that neem twig sales at the Magh Mela are far below what social media videos claim. Several sellers have already left after failing to recover expenses. Others continue to wait in hope of better footfall in the coming days. Vendors advise people not to rely solely on viral content when making business decisions and urge authorities and social media platforms to curb misleading promotional videos. For now, the much-discussed neem twig business remains largely unprofitable on the ground, despite its popularity online.

title: Satua Baba's supercar, Porsche worth ₹4.40 crores:Magh Mela saint with biggest ashram draws political heat and attention amid ongoing UP leadership tensions
summary: Satua Baba is the most talked about at the Magh Mela these days. Baba is seen riding a cart and a camel sometimes, along with his luxury cars. Now, he has left his 3 crore Land Rover Defender and bought a Porsche Turbo 911 sports car. Its price is around 4.40 crores. The car arrived at his camp in Magh Mela on Tuesday night. Here, he performed rituals and received a grand welcome. During this, all the sadhus and saints of Khak Chowk were present. Satua Baba traveled on a cart On Monday, January 12, Satua Baba travelled on a cart. Meanwhile, his 3 crore Defender car drove beside him. During this time, people kept chanting Jai Shri Ram. Satua Baba owns the biggest ashram and the most expensive car Jagadguru Mahamandaleswar Santosh Das alias Satua Baba, the head of Varanasi's Satua Baba Peeth, has been allotted the largest land area in the Magh Mela. The administration has not specified the area covered. Outside his camp in the biggest ashram, his 3 crore luxury car attracts everyone's attention. This is the most expensive car among all the sadhus and saints present at the Magh Mela. Actually, these seemingly ordinary saints are considered close to Yogi Adityanath. Yogi Adityanath himself was present during the conferment of the Jagadguru title. When Yogi was taking a holy dip at the Sangam during the Kumbh Mela, Satya Baba was present with him at that time as well. 57th Acharya of Vishnu Swami Sampradaya, became Jagadguru in Mahakumbh Satua Baba is the head of the Satua Baba Peeth of Vishnu Swami Sampradaya. The head of this sect is known as Satua Baba. In 2012, after the death of the sixth Peethadheeshwar Brahmaleen Yamunacharya Ji Maharaj Satua Baba, this responsibility was given to Santosh Das Ji. Santosh Das Ji became the 57th Acharya of Vishnu Swami Sampradaya. Actually, Santosh Das left his family at the age of 11 and turned towards spirituality. He is also considered a representative of Kashi Vishwanath. Satua Baba was given the title of Jagadguru in Mahakumbh-2025. Politics started before Magh Mela UP politics heated up over Satua Baba after Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya made a remark during an inspection of Magh Mela preparations in Prayagraj. Pointing at a traffic jam, he told officials not to get involved in “Satua Baba’s roti matter,” triggering laughter from officers, including the DM. While leaving, the Deputy CM advised that if any saint or sage demands land, it should be allotted. The comment gained political attention as it came days after the Prayagraj DM was seen baking rotis at Satua Baba’s ashram. DM wearing coat baked roti on the stove Political tension has been ongoing between 2 leaders since 2017 Behind this entire incident is the ongoing political tension between Yogi Adityanath and Keshav Prasad Maurya. After the BJP's big victory in 2017, Keshav Prasad Maurya (then state president) considered himself a contender for the Chief Minister's post. But suddenly, Yogi Adityanath was given the command. This is where the rift began. Keshav was made Deputy Chief Minister, but several major departments (like PWD) were later taken away. In 2022, Keshav lost the Sirathu seat, yet remained Deputy Chief Minister. In 2018-19, letters and allegations between both leaders over PWD tenders and departmental appointments created a tense atmosphere. After the BJP lost 29 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Keshav Maurya's statement further increased the distance between the two. Maurya had said that the organisation is bigger than the government. This was considered an indirect attack on the Yogi government. In 2024-25, both Deputy CMs (Keshav and Brajesh) did not participate in Ayodhya Deepotsav when their names were not printed in the . There were several instances of different statements, like when Keshav distanced himself from Yogi's "Banenge toh Katenge" slogan. Despite past tensions, relations between CM Yogi Adityanath and Keshav Prasad Maurya appeared coordinated in 2025, with both working together during elections. Speaking in Prayagraj on January 10, Yogi warned that division based on caste or religion could push India towards a situation like Bangladesh. He praised Satua Baba for uniting society and said the government would support temple construction at places linked to Jagadguru Ramanandacharya’s legacy. Targeting the opposition, CM Yogi said they are trying to weaken Hinduism under the cover of secularism and remain silent on incidents in Bangladesh, as if their mouths have been sealed. He said the Sangam water is divine, and such moments are possible when a Ram devotee is in power. Highlighting the Sanatan faith, he noted that 31 lakh devotees took a holy dip on Paush Purnima and asserted that the double-engine government is committed to strengthening Sanatan traditions.

title: KGMU conversion case linked to Delhi bomb blast:STF traces medical college records, financial links and radical networks across Agra, Lucknow and multiple states
summary: The investigation into the alleged love jihad and forced conversion case at King George Medical University (KGMU) has revealed connections with the Delhi bomb blast case. Dr. Ramijuddin Nayak, also known as Ramiz Malik, is accused in the KGMU case and has links with Dr. Parvez, co-accused and brother of Dr. Shaheen, the main suspect in the Delhi bomb blast. The Special Task Force (STF) has intensified its probe into these connections. On Tuesday, the STF reached SN Medical College, Agra, to obtain the complete 13-year record of junior and senior resident doctors. Both Dr. Ramiz and Dr. Parvez completed their MBBS from this college. The college principal, Dr. Prashant Gupta, was asked to provide detailed information of all resident doctors from 2012 onwards. STF officials stated that these records will help prepare a comprehensive profile of Dr. Ramiz, identifying his contacts, activities, and potential network. Dr. Ramiz’s hostel stay and influence Dr. Ramiz studied MBBS at SN Medical College from 2012 to 2018 and resided in the hostel between 2013 and 2018. Despite not being selected for postgraduate courses, he continued to live with junior students. STF is investigating the extent of his interactions with these students and any influence he may have exerted. Connection with Dr. Parvez and ‘Islamic Medicos’ group A critical link has emerged with Dr. Parvez, who joined the college for MD in the same year Dr. Ramiz started MBBS. STF alleges that the two created a WhatsApp group named ‘Islamic Medicos’ to allegedly organise Muslim students and attempt conversions of top female students. Investigation led by STF Deputy SP Pramesh Shukla The investigation is being led by STF Deputy SP Pramesh Shukla, who previously dismantled the Chhangur criminal network. Under his supervision, the STF is tracing Dr. Ramiz’s entire network, including associates who may face action in the coming days. Suspicious funding during absconding While absconding, Dr. Ramiz stayed at hotels and with acquaintances in Delhi, Uttarakhand, and Western UP. Bank records show transactions worth millions, including transfers of five to seven lakh rupees to a young man’s account. STF will interrogate the account holder to determine the source and purpose of these funds. Escalation after victim’s attempted suicide The case came to light after a female MD Pathology student at KGMU attempted suicide on 17 December. Her father alleged that Dr. Ramiz trapped his daughter in love jihad, pressuring her to convert to Islam while already being married. In February, he allegedly converted and married another Hindu girl. Action taken by authorities The victim’s father filed complaints with the Chief Minister and the State Women’s Commission. On 22 December, Vice-Chairperson Aparna Yadav held a press conference and assured action. Following a preliminary report by the Visakha Committee, Dr. Ramiz was suspended and banned from campus. An FIR was filed, and a seven-member committee was formed to investigate radical activities at KGMU. The accused doctor’s parents have also been arrested.

title: Report from site where Meerut youth was burnt alive:OBC vs Thakur politics surfaces; aunt says he was returning with ₹80,000 to buy a bike
summary: 'Sonu from Muzaffarnagar was coming to meet me. He called and said, "Auntie, I'm bringing 80 thousand, we'll go buy a bike with brother." That was his last conversation. How was I to know then that Sonu wouldn't be able to meet me? Some auto driver would kill him.' Tears filled the eyes of 60-year-old Madanwati as she spoke about the murder of her nephew, Rohit Kashyap, also known as Sonu. She said Sonu was her elder sister’s son. They last spoke on January 5, and the next day she received the news of his death. According to the police, Sonu was first hit on the head with a brick. Oil was then poured on his body and he was set on fire. The auto driver arrested in the case is a minor and belongs to the Thakur community. After the incident, protests were held in Muzaffarnagar, Lucknow and Delhi. Political parties like the Congress and the Samajwadi Party have raised the issue, calling it a case of OBC versus Thakur. This has led to growing tension and debate over the murder. To understand this, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Ground Zero. Read the full report... Aunt said - We stayed awake all night, he didn't come Jwalagarh is in the Sardhana area of Meerut. Sonu's aunt Madanwati lives here. We reached her house. There was a crowd of people outside the house. Some were offering condolences, some had just come to know how all this happened? We met Madanwati, her husband, sons Sonu, Inder and the villagers. Some leaders of the Kashyap community were also present here. Madanwati's son Sonu said- On January 5, my aunt's son Rohit alias Sonu from Muzaffarnagar was coming to Meerut to meet us. He called saying, 'I am bringing money, help me get a bike.' We kept waiting for him, but he didn't come. At night, he called saying that he had an argument with an auto-rickshaw driver. 'He has snatched my money. He has also made me spend a lot of money. Brother, come save me.' Sought police help, Sonu's mobile switched off After that, we reached the location Sonu told us to save him, but Sonu was not there, nor was any auto driver visible. We got worried, so we went to Salawa police outpost and reported that my aunt's son was missing. He had called and told me some things. The police said - "Okay, we'll look into it." After this, we came home, but Sonu did not return until morning. When we called the number he had given, it was also switched off. Police said - a half-burnt body has been found, come and see it Cousin Sonu said - we wandered all night worried about Rohit alias Sonu, but we couldn't find any trace of him. The next day, I received a call from the police. We were told that a body had been found, come and identify it. We got scared and went with the police to see the body. It was badly burnt. Only some parts of his shoes remained. I was shocked to see them, because they were Sonu's shoes. We told the police that these were the shoes of my aunt's son, Sonu. He was coming to meet us. The police said that they did not find any belongings or money near Sonu's body. Now understand the crime spot A burning body was found outside the school, first seen by the watchman The police found this burnt dead body in the field outside the village's Kisan School. A watchman of the school had seen something burning outside the school that night. Upon going closer to look, he saw a human hand and finger there. The watchman got scared. He immediately called the police and informed them that perhaps someone was burning. The police immediately took the body and surrounding evidence into their custody. Accused dragged Sonu from the road to the field In the field in front of the school, where Sonu Kashyap was burnt, he was dragged for about 50 meters. Police scanned the CCTV cameras installed near the crime spot. At some spots, Sonu and the accused boy were seen together. They were both seen together at a liquor shop, from where they had bought liquor. When the police showed this footage to Sonu's aunt's sons, they identified him. They said that this boy is from the village and is a minor. He drives an auto and belongs to the Thakur community. He plays with the lives of others. He has troubled people before. Police reached the boy's house. After this, he confessed the truth during interrogation. Sonu Kashyap was the sole earner in the family Rohit alias Sonu was only 26 years old. His family includes an elderly mother, who is often ill. He has an eldest sister, who is unmarried. She works in houses. He has an elder brother, who is a respiratory patient. He cannot do any work. His father had died of an illness 6 years ago. Sonu was the only earner in the family. Sonu was the youngest in the house, but the household ran on his earnings. He was not married. The family was looking for a girl for his marriage. Sonu was a confectioner by profession. He had saved some money, with which he was going to buy a bike. But where did that money go, the police are also not telling anything. Sonu's family members say that the police have only arrested one accused and sent him to jail. Whereas others are also involved in this. No one should be spared because of their community. We should get compensation and his sister should get a government job. Now read what the police said about the incident... Fight and murder during drinking alcohol Meerut SSP Dr. Vipin Tada says - The accused auto driver told that he became friends with the boy from Muzaffarnagar in a tempo. After this, both made a plan to drink alcohol. They went to the shop to buy alcohol. Both were seen together in the CCTV footage of the liquor shop. After buying alcohol, both sat at one place and started drinking. During drinking, they had a fight. In this, the youth was killed by hitting him with a brick. Then he was burnt. The accused has been arrested and sent to jail. Now, understand the politics surrounding the entire matter... Jwalagarh is adjacent to Kapsad village Jwalagarh village is adjacent to Kapsad village of Thakur Chaubisi in Sardhana. Kapsad is the same village where on January 8, a young man from the Thakur community murdered Dalit woman Sarita, and then abducted her daughter Ruby. After this, the matter took the form of caste politics. An undeclared curfew was imposed in Kapsad village. Opposition parties created a ruckus due to the girl not being recovered and the accused not being arrested. Many leaders posted messages. They also went to meet the family. The situation deteriorated so much that the police turned the entire village into a cantonment. 60 hours after the kidnapping, the police arrested the accused and safely rescued the victim, Ruby. Now, due to a Thakur vs. OBC case in the adjacent village, politics has started again. In this case too, the accused is a Thakur, while the deceased is an OBC. Former CM Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati, ASPA chief Chandrashekhar, and Congress have raised questions about security. Sardhana MLA and SP leader Atul Pradhan met the victim's family in Jwalagarh on January 11 and offered them condolences. He also provided financial assistance of 1 lakh rupees. Protests from Meerut to Lucknow On January 13, protests took place in this matter from Muzaffarnagar, Meerut to Lucknow. SP workers were dragged. Chandrashekhar was stopped from meeting the victim's family in Muzaffarnagar. On January 12, the victim's family protested at the DM office in Muzaffarnagar and demanded justice. Meanwhile, on January 13, when some SP leaders went to meet the victim's family in Jwalagarh, Meerut, to offer condolences, they were stopped by the police. There was a lot of commotion there. Today, Minister Narendra Kashyap may also come to meet the victim's family.

title: 4 Agra friends found after four days in Ladakh:Car slipped in snow and fell into a 20-feet deep gorge, spent nights stranded before walking 20 km
summary: The location of four friends from Agra who had gone missing in Ladakh for four days has been traced. All four are safe and currently with the Ladakh Police. Their family members have left for Ladakh to bring them back and are expected to return home on Wednesday. According to the Ladakh Police, the four youths had left Pangong Lake by car around 5:30 pm on January 9. They had spoken to their families on the same day, after which all contact was lost. When there was no communication the following day, their families lodged a missing complaint. After a search operation, the police safely located all four. During their journey, the car skidded off the road and fell into a 20-feet-deep ditch. The youths spent the night inside the vehicle. After running out of diesel, they walked nearly 20 kilometres to reach an inhabited area. See 4 pictures of the incident site... Journey from Agra to Ladakh Shivam Chaudhary, a resident of Madhunagar in Agra, had gone on a Ladakh trip with his friends Jaiveer Chaudhary, Yash Mittal, and Sudhanshu Faujdar. The four left Agra by car on January 6 for sightseeing and successfully reached Ladakh. After arriving, they took a new mobile number and stayed in regular contact with their families for two days. On January 9, while at Pangong Lake in Leh, they spoke to their families through a video call. This was the last contact before communication was lost. Family raises alarm, police notified When repeated attempts to contact them failed, the family members filed a missing persons complaint at Sadar Police Station on January 11. Shivam’s father, Daulatram Chaudhary, said that none of the four could be reached, prompting them to inform the police. He confirmed that all four were close friends. Lost route while heading towards Manali Ladakh Police later confirmed that all four youths were safe and released a video of their rescue. The friends endured extreme conditions over three days while struggling to survive. January 9 -At around 5 pm, they spoke to their families and then left Pangong Lake for Leh. Near Kharu, they noticed a signboard pointing towards Manali and mistakenly took that route. January 10 -They halted at Pang. January 11 -They resumed their journey towards Manali, but the road ahead was closed. After crossing Sarchu, they turned back. Near Nakila, their car slipped and fell about 20 feet into snow. Fortunately, the vehicle did not overturn. They stayed inside the car, using the heater for warmth. January 12- They spent another day in the car. When the diesel ran out, they decided to walk towards the nearby huts they had noticed earlier. January 13- After walking approximately 20 kilometres, they reached a hut near Whiskey Nala, where the Ladakh Police located and rescued them. They were then brought back to Leh. Police confirmation Agra ACP Sadar, Imran Ahmed, stated that the families were advised to contact Leh-Ladakh Police. Information received confirmed that all four youths had been found safely. He said communication was disrupted due to poor network connectivity caused by bad weather. The matter is currently under investigation.

title: Lavish lives of Kinnar Akharas grab eyeballs at Magh Mela:VIP convoys to luxury makeup rituals, kinnars show mix of glamour power
summary: For the first time in the history of the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, two transgender akharas have taken their place in the festival, creating a striking presence. At the heart of this world is the Kinnar Akhara pavilion, where visitors are greeted by another side of the mela. The first group — Kinnar Akhara — is led by Mahamandaleshwar Lakshmi Narayan Tripathi, while the newly formed Sanatan Kinnar Akhara is guided by Mahamandaleshwar Kaushalya Nand Giri, popularly known as Tina Maa. Stepping inside, you see a glamorous lifestyle in full display. Transgender participants move through VIP protocol entry with security guards both in front and behind, flanked by female bouncers. SUVs like Fortuners and Thars are lined up for their transportation. Members say they spend two to three hours getting ready to feel something divine, drawing inspiration from Shiva’s form of Ardhanarishvara. To understand the lifestyle of transgenders, Dainik Bhaskar team reached Sanatan Kinnar Akhada. Read the Ground Report... Convoy with sirens, gunner deployed for security Our team was present outside the akhada when suddenly the attendants started clearing the crowd. A siren sound is heard from one side, within 10 minutes a convoy of vehicles like Fortuner and Innova stops outside the akhada, showing 4 to 5 vehicles. Mahamandaleshwar Kaushalya Nand Giri (Teena Maa) steps out from inside. People standing nearby rush to touch her feet. Very simply, she blesses everyone and goes inside the akhada. The gunner and bouncers also follow her inside. Teena Maa sits on a throne in the main pavilion, after which the process of giving blessings begins. Kausalya Nand Giri says - We transgenders face discrimination everywhere in society. When family members expelled me in childhood, I reached the guru, and from there life found its purpose. 3 hours of makeup, then worship Lord Shiva From here we reached the Kinnar Akhada at Sangam Lower Road. We found that Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Dr. Lakshmi Narayan Tripathi was not here, but more than 400 transgender saints were present. Here we met Mahamandaleshwar Kankeshwari Maharaj. She was sitting with tripund and red bindi on her forehead. She says that kinnar look good only in makeup. We do makeup for our Lord. Usually when people see our makeup, they ask if we carry a makeup artist with us? My answer is that we don't have enough money to carry a makeup artist. We have learned to do our own makeup. "The Mahamandleshwar dresses up like a bride every day. It takes 3 hours. Then we worship Lord Shiva with this same appearance. We remain absorbed in worship and prayer of Bholenath for 4 hours. All this continues for 7 hours," she said. Wearing jewelry worth Rs 50 lakhs, iPhone in hands During the discussion about adornment, we asked Kankeshwari Maharaj about their jewelry. They were wearing 6 gold rings studded with diamonds and rubies on their fingers. Four thick gold chains were visible around the neck. Their value was around Rs 50 lakhs, and they had an expensive iPhone in hand. Why do you wear so much makeup? Smiling, she answered, "We wear makeup for our God and our guru. Our guru is our parents, our God. We have a great passion for dressing up. That's why we do our own makeup." Who do you worship? She said, "Our day begins with the worship of Bauchara Maa. I perform worship for about an hour. I am Ardhanarishwar, so I worship Lord Shiva as my deity." 'Had to separate from family at the age of 8' UP Kinnar Welfare Board member Mahamandaleshwar Kankeshwari says, "When I was 8 years old, I got separated from my family. I also had to face society's rejection. My father worked as a guard in railways in Kolkata, but according to social customs, they separated us and I became an orphan." No parents want to separate from their child. But looking at society, we had to separate from our families. She says - The same society that once rejected us has now accepted us. Today people are coming to us for blessings," she added. Mahamandaleshwar from Nashik says, 'We perform yoni worship' Here, Pooja Nand Giri, the Mahamandaleshwar of Kinnar Akhada from Nashik, Maharashtra, was seen performing puja with her transgender disciples. She said - We have set up Mata Kamakhya's Yoni Kund. We perform yoni worship here for about 1.5 to 2 hours daily. We perform puja here for those who don't have children and those who are unable to get married. Rituals are also being performed here for the welfare of the country. The time from 7 PM to 8:30 PM has been specifically designated for this puja. After coming here, we learned that most saints of the akhada don't go out among people without makeup. Daily worship of Mother Kamakhya's yoni is performed in the camp. Transgenders have lakhs of followers on Insta-Facebook Transgender Akhada's Mahamandaleshwar Kausalya Nand Giri (Choti Maa) remains in discussions mostly for her reels on social media. She creates reels in new styles and uploads them on her Instagram. She has more than 5.45 lakh followers on Instagram. Her reels go viral frequently, sometimes showing her on a moving boat or waving a trident in her hands. Sometimes appears dressed in a sari doing bridal-like roles. They have hired 2 experts for making reels, who create reels in different attractive looks. Similarly, Palak who is associated with Sanatani Kinnar Akhada also likes to make reels. She also has more than 77 thousand followers on Instagram. She creates and posts her videos in different looks each time. Funds come from devotees' offerings and temple area It is natural to wonder where the money comes from for such a luxurious lifestyle. Actually, thousands of people approach transgenders for blessings. Whoever seeks their blessing does not go empty-handed. People willingly and respectfully offer them gifts according to their means. During Mahakumbh, long queues of people would form at the transgender akhada for hours. Wealthy people also make generous donations out of devotion. People stand in line to receive blessings from Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Dr. Lakshmi Narayan Tripathi. The Mahamandaleshwars who are appointed to the akhada are assigned jurisdiction over a city or major temple area. Perception towards transgenders changed through Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Kinnar Akhada's Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Dr. Lakshmi Narayan Tripathi has written 2 books about third genders. The first book is 'Me Hijra- Me Lakshmi'. It is available in Hindi, Marathi, English and Gujarati. Similarly, the second book is 'The Red Lipstick Men in My Life'. Acharya says that these books reveal the real world of transgenders. This has also changed people's perception towards transgenders. People make sarcastic remarks, but it doesn't affect me. A German production made a film 'Third Gender Between the Lines' about transgenders. Similarly, Akshay Kumar's film 'Laxmi' also showed the struggle of transgenders. Lakshmi Narayan Tripathi supported it as a brand ambassador. She also did branding for this film with Akshay Kumar.

title: Manikarnika Ghat demolition sparks backlash across Madhya Pradesh:Khasgi Trust demands probe and restoration, protests erupt; Patwari calls it 'attack' on Ahilyabai's legacy
summary: The Khasgi Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Charities Trust has strongly condemned the demolition of a section of the historic Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh calling the action deeply disrespectful to India’s cultural and spiritual heritage and to the legacy of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. In a formal statement, the Trust said it was ‘shocked and outraged’ by the demolition of the ghat, which was first restored by Devi Ahilyabai Holkar in 1791 and held special significance for her. Among hundreds of sites she built or restored across the country, Manikarnika Ghat was one of the rare locations where she had installed effigies in her own image, depicting her worshipping the sacred river Ganga. Jitu Patwari slams BJP, calls it attack on Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy Madhya Pradesh Congress Committee chief Jitu Patwari has strongly criticised the BJP over the demolition of a section of the historic Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi, calling it a direct assault on the legacy of Lokmata Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. In a post on social media platform X, Patwari said that in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s parliamentary constituency of Kashi, the BJP government had demolished a heritage structure built by Devi Ahilyabai Holkar in 1771. He alleged that a government which seeks votes in the name of culture and Sanatan traditions is now erasing temples and heritage sites associated with Ahilyabai Holkar. Congress staged protest at Gandhi Statue in Indore Meanwhile, the Congress party staged a protest against the demolition. Former minister Sajjan Singh Verma staged a sit-in protest from 5 pm to 6 pm on Wednesday at the Ahilyabai Holkar statue site at Rajwada, Indore, against the alleged demolition of Ahilya Ghat, the statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar, and associated temple structures in Varanasi. Demolition carried out without prior notice According to the Trust, the demolition was carried out on January 10, allegedly on instructions from municipal authorities, without prior notice or warning, and the structure was razed within hours. The Trust said the action showed complete disregard for the ghat’s historical, religious, and cultural importance . The Khasgi Trust, along with the Holkar royal family of Indore, has said the sacred effigies of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar now lie buried in debris. The Trust has initiated steps to recover the damaged idols and is preparing legal action against the agencies responsible, asserting its role as the principal custodian of Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy and of Manikarnika Ghat . Questions over heritage law violations Experts have raised serious concerns over possible violations of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958, which provides strict legal protection to historic monuments. The Act empowers the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to regulate activities around heritage sites, including enforcing a 100-metre prohibited zone and a 200-metre regulated zone to prevent unauthorised construction or demolition. Amendments introduced in 2010 further tightened restrictions on any activity near protected monuments. Legal and heritage experts argue that any intervention at a site like Manikarnika Ghat should have followed a clearly defined process involving ASI permissions and heritage impact assessments. Historians flag cultural loss Historians point out that Manikarnika Ghat houses at least 21 temples, dharamshalas, annakshetras, and bathing ghats, many of which were built or restored under Devi Ahilyabai Holkar’s supervision. Ansari added that while the government has issued commemorative coins and memoirs to mark the 300th birth anniversary of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar, the demolition sends a contradictory message. Protests and anger in Indore The demolition has sparked anger in Indore, where members of the Dhangar, Pal, Baghel, and other communities have announced a meeting on January 15 to chalk out protest strategies. Community representatives said the action is particularly painful as it comes during the concluding phase of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar’s 300th birth anniversary celebrations, calling it an insult to her memory and contributions. As demands grow for accountability and restoration, the Manikarnika Ghat demolition has reignited a broader debate over heritage protection versus development, and whether India’s most sacred sites are being altered without due regard for history, law, and faith.

title: Fog disrupts visibility in UP, youth killed on Muzaffarnagar highway:19 cities colder than Shimla; rain alert issued for 3 days
summary: Uttar Pradesh continues to reel under intense cold as icy winds push temperatures to record lows. On Wednesday morning, dense fog blanketed at least 25 districts, including Meerut and Sambhal, severely reducing visibility. Because of poor visibility, a speeding vehicle rammed into a motorcycle late Tuesday night in Muzaffarnagar. The biker died on the spot. Due to dense fog and darkness, vehicles kept running over the body throughout the night. A police patrol team noticed the body in the morning and sent it to the hospital for post-mortem. In a separate incident in Shahjahanpur, four youths riding a motorcycle were injured after being hit by a speeding vehicle. All of them were on their way to work at a brick kiln when the accident occurred. Temperatures in 19 cities drop below Shimla Over the past 24 hours, the minimum temperature in 19 cities across the state fell below Shimla’s 6.6°C. Muzaffarnagar recorded the lowest temperature at 2.1°C. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for the next three days. Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said that two western disturbances will become active in the state from January 15. This is expected to raise minimum temperatures by 3 to 5°C. Cold wave conditions in western Uttar Pradesh may gradually ease, but dense fog is likely to continue. Light to moderate rainfall is expected in some areas between January 18 and 20. Cold persist in Lucknow, schools remain closed In Lucknow, light fog and haze were observed on Wednesday morning. Icy winds blowing at around 13 kmph increased the chill. Due to severe cold, schools up to Class 8 have been closed in Noida and Chandauli till January 15, and in Jhansi till January 14. In Ghaziabad, schools up to Class 5 will remain closed till January 15. See pictures..

title: SP MLA slams BJP leader Sangeet Som:Claims he is a meat trader in Meerut; questions documents backing the accusation made public
summary: Sangeet Som, MLA from Sardhana in Meerut, UP, is back in the news. He recently demanded the removal of Mustafizur Rahman from Shah Rukh Khan's IPL team, KKR. Known as a firebrand leader, Som has now come under attack from Sardhana’s current SP MLA, Atul Pradhan, who questioned his past record. Pradhan also shared documents related to Som’s history, raising questions about whether he was involved in the meat business. If true, people want to know which companies he worked with, what positions he held, for how long, and what the current situation is? In this Dainik Bhaskar report, know all the facts related to Sangeet Som's business Director for two and a half years at Al Dua Food Processing Private Limited According to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs records, Sangeet Singh Som served as a director in Al Dua Food Processing Private Limited company from December 22, 2005, to March 27, 2008. His association with the company began in 2005 when he co-founded the company with Moinuddin Qureshi and Yogesh Rawat. He served as a director of the company. In 2005-06, the company also received an unsecured loan of 4 lakh rupees. Al-Dua company is primarily involved in the export of buffalo, sheep, goat meat, and hides. It supplies to Arab countries. Som held this position until March 2008, when he transferred his 20,000 shares to Naseera Begum. Additionally, Som was also an additional director in another company named Al-Anam Agro Foods Private Limited. This was also associated with Moinuddin Qureshi. Director in several companies including Tejas Oil Company According to documents, Sangeet Som is still a director in Tejas Oil Company Private Limited, which works for the processing and preservation of meat, fish, fruits, vegetables, oil, and fat. Apart from Tejas, Som has a record of directorship in Blooming Build Tech Private Limited, Baba Fabrication Private Limited, Tejshita Builders Private Limited, and Tej Film Production Private Limited companies. This means Sangeet Singh Som has considerable experience working as a director in the meat business, civil work, and film production companies. Sangeet Som was a director in Yamuna Beverage Private Limited company from February 2011 to December 2016. The work of this company was wine manufacturing. Wife also a Director in multiple meat companies Other members of Sangeet Som's family have also been directors in companies involved in the meat business. Among them, Sangeet Som's wife, Simran Thakur, is reported to be associated with 7 companies. This includes the meat trading company Tejas Oil, along with Jai Sai Food Beverage Private Limited, Tejarshita Builders Private Limited, and Shri Hans Glasses Private Limited. Besides these, she has also been a Director in Yamuna Beverage and Baba Fabrication. Allegations of Meat Supply and Land Grabbing Recently, Samajwadi Party MLA Atul Pradhan made a big accusation against Sangeet Som. He said that Som is associated with a meat processing company. Atul also accused Som of illegally occupying the land of the poor and encroaching on government property. He stated that Som's companies have encroached upon government land worth approximately 66 crore rupees. To occupy these lands, Sangeet Som misused the security provided by the central government, on which crores of rupees are spent every year. Pradhan questioned Som's Hindutva image, calling him a 'hypocrite'. He said, "The person who calls himself the Hindu heart emperor and gives inflammatory statements against Muslims, is himself involved in the meat business." Pradhan demanded that Som's security be withdrawn and an investigation be initiated against him. Is there a political rivalry, what is the complete equation of the seat? Sardhana assembly seat is one of the hot seats in Western UP. The total number of voters here is around 3.5 lakh. Talking about caste equations, the number of Muslims here is around 85 to 90 thousand. The number of Thakurs is 60 to 65 thousand and the number of Dalits is 40 to 45 thousand. Besides this, Jats, Gurjars, Brahmin Tyagis also live in good numbers in this area. Sangeet Som won elections from here in 2012 and 2017. However, in 2022, Gurjar leader Atul Pradhan defeated him. Sangeet Som was defeated by 18,200 votes. Since then, a political rivalry has been ongoing between the two leaders. Recently, the Kapsad incident, in which a Dalit mother and daughter were attacked. The mother was murdered and the daughter was abducted. As this matter gained momentum, politics also began. Atul Pradhan stood in favor of the victim Dalit family. Following that, Atul held a press conference and made serious allegations against Sangeet Som.
