title: 'Indestructible Kashi itself will become cause of BJP’s-destruction'- Akhilesh Yadav:Priyanka calls Manikarnika Ghat demolition grave sin
summary: The demolition and redevelopment work at Manikarnika Ghat, one of the most sacred cremation grounds in Kashi, has triggered a major political controversy. The Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) have strongly criticised the BJP-led government, alleging that centuries-old religious and cultural heritage is being destroyed in the name of development. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said that “indestructible Kashi itself will become the cause of BJP’s destruction”, accusing the ruling party of acting purely for monetary gain. Sharp questions raised by Priyanka Gandhi Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party president Mallikarjun Kharge also raised sharp questions over the project. Controversy regarding ₹25 crore redevelopment project First see 2 pictures... Priyanka Gandhi: “Erasing Cultural Identity” Priyanka Gandhi wrote on X that it was “extremely unfortunate” to run bulldozers over a centuries-old religious and cultural site like Manikarnika Ghat. She said the ghat holds immense religious significance and is deeply linked to the legacy of Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar. Calling the demolition a “grave sin”, Priyanka alleged that heritage sites are being destroyed for the commercial benefit of a few. She further claimed that several ancient temples in Banaras had already been demolished earlier in the name of renovation and warned that attempts to erase Kashi’s religious, spiritual and cultural identity must stop immediately. Kharge questions the PM Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge directly questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi, asking whether business interests were driving such redevelopment projects. He posed two questions on behalf of the public. First, could renovation and beautification not have been carried out while preserving the original heritage? He cited examples such as the removal of statues of Mahatma Gandhi and Dr B R Ambedkar from Parliament premises and changes made to the Jallianwala Bagh Memorial. Second, Kharge asked why centuries-old statues were reduced to debris instead of being preserved in a museum. Referring to the Prime Minister’s earlier remarks on the Ganga, Kharge said the ghats of Banaras are the city’s identity and questioned whether public access to them was being compromised. He also raised concerns for devotees who come to Kashi in their final days seeking salvation. Akhilesh Yadav’s attack Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of showing disrespect towards the legacy of Rajmata Punyashlok Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. He said no true believer would tolerate insult to her statues or to Kashi’s Sanatani heritage. According to Akhilesh, the BJP neither cares for Kashi nor its residents, nor for the historical personalities associated with it. He claimed greed was the sole motive behind the project. How the controversy began... Project Background Prime Minister Modi laid the foundation stone for the redevelopment project in 2023. Work was halted for around 18 months due to floods and has now resumed at a faster pace. Both Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghats are being redeveloped. The permanent ghat structure was demolished using heavy machinery, following which allegations emerged that a 300-year-old stone structure had been removed. Ahilyabai Trust Raises Objections Yashwant Holkar, chairman of the Maharani Ahilyabai Trust, visited Gurudham Temple to perform purification rituals before broken statues of the queen. He said four statues installed at the corners of Manikarnika Ghat’s shrine were damaged, with two found broken. Calling the act unforgivable, he said the Indore royal family had never imagined such treatment of Ahilyabai’s legacy in Kashi. The Trust has demanded that missing parts of the statues be returned within seven days and insisted that redevelopment cannot proceed without its consent, citing Supreme Court-granted conservation rights. Dom Raja Family Dismisses Claims Vishwanath Chaudhary of Kashi’s Dom Raja family rejected allegations of idol destruction, calling them misleading. He said beautification of the ghat was requested by his own family and approved by the Prime Minister. He added that idols had been safely removed and would be reinstalled at their original locations after completion of work, emphasising that an organised and well-maintained ghat serves the interest of devotees from across India and abroad.

title: Sword distribution accused Pinky Chaudhary welcomed with massive rally:Slogan shouting traffic violations seen as convoy of SUVs moves through Ghaziabad
summary: A major procession took place outside Dasna Jail in Ghaziabad on Thursday, following the release of Hindu Raksha Dal’s national president Pinky Chaudhary and her son Harsh Chaudhary. Hundreds of supporters gathered as the leaders were freed in a case related to the distribution of swords. The convoy, stretching up to 20 km, saw boys hanging from car windows and fireworks being set off. Vehicles in the procession included multiple SUVs such as Scorpios, Thars, and Fortuners. Now see 4 pictures... Grand Procession from Jail to Office Immediately after their release, Pinky Chaudhary led a procession from Dasna Jail to the Hindu Raksha Dal office in Shalimar Garden. She recorded a video from a moving car, saying: “Ram… Ram, we have come from jail. We will do religious work again. My companions are taking me, you also see.” The video shows supporters leaning out of cars, chanting slogans, and honking as they moved through the city. At the office, Chaudhary met with party workers, receiving a hero’s welcome from supporters. Bail granted after sword distribution case Pinky Chaudhary had filed a bail application in Ghaziabad district court for a case related to distributing swords door-to-door. On 14 January, the court accepted her bail, and the release was processed the following day. During her release, Chaudhary also recorded videos of the convoy celebrating her return. Swords distributed in Ghaziabad The controversy traces back to 29 September 2025, when a 21-second video surfaced showing Hindu Raksha Dal members distributing swords and axes in Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad. The recipients were told the weapons were for the protection of their sisters and daughters, and to defend themselves in case of a situation like Bangladesh. Each sword was touched to the forehead, followed by chants of “Jai Shri Ram”. Following the video, police arrested Pinky Chaudhary and her son on 6 January, along with 10 others. Even those who unknowingly received swords, including a society guard, were taken into custody. Mixed reactions from locals Some recipients of the swords claim they were unaware of the consequences. Bhavana, whose husband was given a sword at home, said: “He has no connection with them. There is an atmosphere of fear. Everyone should have weapons. Look at what is happening in Bangladesh. We are not safe here.” Another local, Amit, who had a brother among those arrested, stated: “We had nothing to do with this. Just because something happened elsewhere doesn’t mean it will happen here. The organisation is doing wrong, and there should be no talk of Hindu-Muslim or caste issues.” Pinky Chaudhary and family defend actions In a video posted on 3 January, Pinky Chaudhary said she would respond strongly to any cases filed against her. Her daughter, Karuna Chaudhary, justified the sword distribution, claiming that “every house should have a Pinky Chaudhary for the safety of sisters and daughters.” Organisation’s history of controversies Hindu Raksha Dal has a long record of controversies. The group has previously been involved in attacks on Muslims, communal sloganeering, and issuing inflammatory statements. After the Pahalgam terror attack, the organisation released a video threatening Kashmiri Muslims in Dehradun. In August 2024, Pinky Chaudhary and others allegedly attacked Muslims in a Ghaziabad slum, calling them Bangladeshis. Cases were registered, and she was arrested but later released on bail. In August 2021, Chaudhary had also made communal statements during a rally at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, resulting in brief detention.

title: First newborn girl in family sparks huge celebration in Hamirpur:13 Scorpio convoy, DJ drums mark joyous arrival
summary: A family marked the birth of a baby girl with an elaborate celebration, taking out a convoy of 13 Scorpio SUVs in Hamirpur. The cars, decorated with blue balloons, moved along the highway with DJ music, band and drum beats, as family members danced and sang their way home. On reaching home, the women of the family gave the newborn a grand welcome with band music. Baby girl born on Tuesday The baby girl was born on Tuesday, and her arrival is special as a daughter was born in the family after one generation. A video of the celebration has also surfaced. The incident is from Mohalla Fattepur in Maudaha town. First see 3 pictures... Family waited years for a daughter Anjum Parvez alias Raju lives in Mohalla Fattepur, Maudaha. His father is a retired Army personnel, while Raju runs a flour mill from home. His wife’s name is Nikhat Fatima. Raju is the eldest of four brothers and has no sisters. The other brothers are unmarried. The family had been hoping for the birth of a daughter for a long time. Baby girl born two days ago Nikhat Fatima was admitted to a hospital about one kilometre from home for delivery. On Tuesday night, she gave birth to a baby girl. As soon as the doctors informed the family, their happiness knew no bounds. After Nikhat was discharged, the family decided to celebrate the occasion in a big way. A convoy of 13 Scorpios travelled from the hospital to their home, all decorated with balloons. DJ music, drum beats and dancing accompanied the long line of vehicles throughout the journey. Raju and Nikhat travelled in one vehicle with their newborn, while other cars carried relatives and family members. Neighbours also joined the celebrations on their arrival. Grandfather blesses granddaughter with ₹5,000 The baby’s grandfather and family elder, Ruknuddin, a retired BSF personnel, welcomed his granddaughter by giving a blessing of ₹5,000. Holding the baby in his lap, he said the little girl had brought happiness and prosperity to the family. “All my illness disappeared,” says grandmother The baby’s grandmother, Roshni, expressed her joy, saying that all her illness seemed to have vanished with the arrival of her granddaughter. She said the birth of the girl had brought new energy and happiness into the household, especially as the family had waited so long for a daughter. Doctor calls it a rare and positive example Dr Anshu Mishra, from the hospital where Nikhat delivered, said that in the last three years in Hamirpur district, she had not seen such an open and enthusiastic celebration for the birth of a girl child. She added that such celebrations can help change social attitudes, sending a strong message that daughters are not a burden, but a source of pride and happiness.

title: Cockroach spotted in noodles at Lucknow’s Robot Restaurant:Children panic during birthday party; family alleges negligence from management
summary: A cockroach was found in a plate of noodles at Lucknow’s well-known Robot Restaurant in Aliganj on Wednesday evening. A birthday party was underway at the restaurant when the incident occurred. The family had ordered noodles for children, and a cockroach was spotted immediately while the dish was being served. Family raises issue with manager The family raised the issue with the restaurant manager. However, instead of accepting responsibility, the manager initially offered to replace the noodles in an apparent attempt to downplay the matter. This further upset the family, who later complained with the Food and Drug Administration (FSDA). Now read the full matter in detail... Cockroach spotted while noodles were being served According to the complainant, Ashutosh, it was his daughter’s birthday on Wednesday. He had reached the Robot Restaurant in Aliganj with family members and friends in the evening. After placing orders, noodles were served for the children. As the noodles were being placed on the children’s plates, a cockroach was clearly visible in one of the servings. Ashutosh said the children were frightened on seeing the cockroach, and the family panicked. He added that the situation could have turned serious if a child had accidentally consumed the contaminated food. Family upset by manager’s response Ashutosh said he immediately complained to the restaurant manager, but the response was disappointing. The manager allegedly tried to brush aside the issue and suggested resolving it by placing a fresh order. This response angered the family members. Although the manager later apologised, the family said they were deeply hurt by the initial attitude and handling of the complaint. Complaint lodged with Food Safety Department Ashutosh has filed a formal complaint with the Food Safety and Drug Administration regarding the incident. He has demanded strict action against the restaurant, stating that negligence of this kind poses a serious risk to public health and should not be taken lightly. Incident raises concerns over food safety monitoring Other customers present at the restaurant at the time also expressed their displeasure. Many said such negligence was unexpected from a large and modern establishment like Robot Restaurant. The incident has raised serious questions about the restaurant’s hygiene standards as well as the effectiveness of food safety monitoring by the authorities.

title: 8-year-old son gets mother’s post-mortem done in Etah:Sits cries beside her body; says, 'Relatives will kill me'
summary: In Etah, Uttar Pradesh, an eight-year-old boy was seen sitting beside his mother’s body during her post-mortem, crying inconsolably as he looked at her shroud-covered corpse and wiped his tears. The scene moved policemen and others present, with one person consoling the child by placing a hand on his shoulder. The boy’s father, who was HIV-positive, died a year ago, and his mother has now also died of the same disease, leaving the child alone. With no one initially coming forward to carry the body, relatives arrived only after 17 hours, allowing the inquest to be completed. An inspector has taken responsibility for performing the woman’s last rites. The child has also expressed fear for his life, alleging a threat from his own relatives. He said, 'My family members want to usurp my land. My life is in danger.' See Photos... Case details The case is from Nagla Dheeraj village in Jaithra police station area. A 45-year-old woman lived at home with her 8-year-old son and 13-year-old daughter. A year ago, her husband died of HIV. Since then, the woman was also ill. For 8 days, the woman was undergoing treatment at Veerangana Avanti Bai Medical College. She passed away at 10 PM on January 14. After his mother's death, the eight-year-old son reached the district headquarters alone at 7 AM with his mother's body for a post-mortem. Child sat crying in front of his mother's dead body He sat on the floor beside his mother’s body in the post-mortem house, sobbing continuously. Police waited to prepare the inquest report, but even five people were not available as witnesses. After receiving information, some relatives arrived around 3 pm, following which the post-mortem process began. Expressed threat to life from family The child said, No member of his family has come forward to help him. Everyone is after his 5 bigha property. He fears for his life from his family. Treated mother alone, even in Delhi The son stated that ever since his mother fell ill, he had been solely responsible for her treatment. He took his mother for treatment to Lohia Hospital in Farrukhabad, Hallett Hospital in Kanpur, and even to Delhi. For about eight days, his mother's health had significantly worsened, leading to her admission to Veerangana Avantibai Medical College in Etah. No one cared for ailing mother Ultimately, the mother passed away during treatment. The son claims that despite knowing about his mother's illness, no relative or kin bothered to check on her. Now, upon receiving the news of his mother's death, other family members, including his uncle, arrived. Revenue officials have been dispatched for the last rites, which will be conducted under the supervision of the administration. Jaithra Police Station in-charge Ritesh Thakur has taken charge of the deceased woman's last rites.

title: Transgender leader Sonam Chishti attacked in UP:Gunpoint abduction, beating forced haircut alleged; CM Yogi urged to intervene
summary: Transgender leader Sonam Chishti, who held the rank of Minister of State in the Yogi Adityanath government, was allegedly kidnapped at gunpoint, assaulted and forcibly had her hair cut in Uttar Pradesh’s Ghazipur district. The incident reportedly took place when she had gone to collect congratulatory offerings along with members of the transgender community. The state president of the transgender community has demanded strict action from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging police inaction and refusal to register a complaint. Incident reported from Ghazipur police station area According to Iqbal Kinnar, state president of the transgender community, the incident occurred on the night of November 28. He said Sonam Chishti, a former minister of state rank, had come to meet him and later accompanied his group to collect congratulatory gifts at a wedding in the Ghazipur area, a traditional practice within the community. Group of 20 men allegedly attacked, Sonam taken away Iqbal alleged that while they were returning, transgenders from a rival group, accompanied by around 20 men armed with sticks and pistols, surrounded them and launched an attack. Two transgenders were seriously injured, one of whom suffered a fractured hand and is undergoing treatment in Kanpur. During the assault, Sonam Chishti was allegedly abducted and taken away. Iqbal claimed she was later found unconscious and abandoned. Allegation of police refusing to register complaint Iqbal Kinnar said complaints were submitted to the District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police, alleging that outsiders were falsely changing their gender identity, attacking local transgender leaders and forcefully taking over their positions. He claimed the police station refused to accept their complaint, prompting an appeal to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for justice. Police deny receiving any complaint Station in-charge Hanuman Pratap Singh said the police had no information about the incident. He stated that no written complaint had been received so far and assured that appropriate action would be taken once a complaint is filed. What the viral video shows In the video linked to the incident, a transgender person holding scissors identifies herself as Sanya Nayak from the Bilanda area of Ghazipur. She is seen questioning another transgender person, who identifies herself as Sonam Nayak. Sonam is seated on a cot with two transgenders sitting beside her, while another person standing behind forcibly cuts her hair with scissors. It is claimed that Sonam had come from Sultanpur along with Iqbal and Babli Nayak. Who Is Sonam Chishti? Previous controversies and public statements Sonam Chishti has previously made headlines for questioning her own party in Bareilly, alleging that bulldozers were being used against the homes of the poor. During a meeting in Kanpur, she had threatened to resign, stating that issues faced by the transgender community were being ignored. In Aligarh, she had demanded the scrapping of pensions for MPs and MLAs. She had also sought a BJP ticket from Sultanpur ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, but the party fielded Maneka Gandhi, who eventually lost to the Samajwadi Party candidate.

title: 'I don’t want an impotent man,' says wife:Kanpur man ends life after consuming poison at in-laws’ doorstep; married 2.5 years ago
summary: In Kanpur, a young man died by suicide after consuming poison outside his in-laws’ house in the Chakeri police station area. He had gone to persuade his wife, but she shut the door on him and did not respond despite repeated knocking. At around 3:40 pm on Wednesday, he made a final call to his wife, which went unanswered. After this, the man consumed poison in his auto and returned home, where his condition worsened. He was taken to Kanshiram Hospital and later referred to Hallett Hospital, where doctors declared him dead late Wednesday night. According to the police, the couple had been in a relationship for 8 years. Two and a half years ago, they got married in a temple. Four months ago, after an argument with her husband, the wife had gone to her parental home. The WhatsApp chat between the husband and wife has come to light. In it, the wife wrote to her husband, I don't want a coward, a cheater like you. I hate... you, your name, your hypocritical actions. Is this the first time you're eating outside food because of me? Complete story of love, marriage, and suicide, read in 4 points 1. Married without family’s consent: Vikram Kewat (25), an auto driver from Anand Vihar under Hanumant Vihar police station area, was the only son of Jai Kumar, who lives with his wife Isha and four daughters, Chinchhi, Pooja, Sanno and Shalu. Vikram had been in a relationship with Riya, a resident of Ramadevi’s Delhi Pulia, for eight years. About two-and-a-half years ago, they married in a temple without informing the family, and later lived in a rented house in Damodar Nagar. The father alleged Riya never allowed the family to meet Vikram. 2. Contact cut off after marriage: Jai Kumar said Riya blocked the family’s numbers on Vikram’s phone. After marriage, domestic disputes arose, and about four months ago Riya left Vikram and went to her parental home. Despite repeated attempts, Vikram was unable to persuade her to return. 3. Repeated suicide attempts alleged: According to the father, Vikram, distressed by marital issues, had attempted suicide four to five times earlier. About 15 days ago, Riya allegedly came to their Damodar Nagar house, took jewellery and Rs 1 lakh in cash, and returned to her maternal home. Vikram later found his number blocked again. 4. Poison consumed after call unanswered: Jai Kumar said that on Wednesday, around 3 pm, Vikram went by auto to Riya’s house to convince her, but she did not open the door. At 3:40 pm, he called her again, but the call went unanswered. Vikram then consumed poison in his parked auto. Around 4:15 pm, he returned home, where his condition worsened. He was taken to Kanshiram Hospital and later referred to Hallett Hospital, where he died late at night. Husband and wife argued on WhatsApp After Vikram's death, his family checked his mobile. They found some WhatsApp messages showing an argument between Vikram and Riya. Chakeri Police Station in-charge Ajay Prakash Mishra said, The body has been sent for post-mortem. The family has not yet filed a complaint.

title: ASP Anuj Chaudhary arrives in Gorakhpur, offers prayers at temple:Yogi presents khichdi, smiles as child asks for chips
summary: CM Yogi offered khichdi at the Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur on Thursday morning, marking the occasion of Makar Sankranti. Gorakshapitheshwar Yogi Adityanath entered the sanctum sanctorum at around 3:40 a.m. and, following the Nath tradition, performed special worship and rituals in honour of Guru Gorakhnath. He blew the traditional whistle hanging around his neck and bowed in reverence. After the rituals, khichdi was offered to Guru Gorakhnath, including the sacred offering sent by the Nepal Royal Family. CM tours temple premises Following the worship, the Chief Minister toured the temple premises and extended Makar Sankranti greetings to devotees. Soon after, the ritual of common devotees offering khichdi formally began. Temple echoes with sounds of drums On the festival day, lakhs of devotees from Nepal, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar thronged the Gorakhnath Temple. The entire temple complex echoed with the sound of drums and devotional chants. By 8 am, around three lakh devotees had already offered khichdi. Long queues were seen outside the temple, with devotees getting darshan after waiting for nearly an hour. See the pictures... Devotees offer khichdi Due to the massive crowd, many devotees were offering khichdi from outside the sanctum sanctorum. With hundreds of people offering rice, lentils, sesame seeds and other ingredients simultaneously, it appeared as though grains were raining across the temple premises. Devotees from Nepal to participate Thousands of devotees arrived from Nepal to participate in the ritual. They said offering khichdi at Gorakhnath Temple on Makar Sankranti is an age-old tradition in their country, as Baba Gorakhnath is regarded as their revered deity. To manage the crowd and ensure smooth arrangements, temple volunteers along with police and administrative personnel were deployed at various points across the premises.

title: Husband, wife found running sex racket from Varanasi house:Man flees during police raid, spouse arrested; boys, girls found unclothed
summary: A husband and wife were allegedly operating a sex racket from their residence in Varanasi, using a spa centre as a cover. The operation was busted after police conducted a raid on Wednesday. During the raid, several young men and women were found without clothes. Two young men and a young woman were caught in objectionable circumstances, and multiple objectionable items were recovered from one of the rooms. Police forced open the doors of two rooms and arrested the spa centre owner along with two women and two men. Investigations revealed that the spa was being run jointly by the woman and her husband. However, the accused husband managed to escape from the spot during the police action. The spa centre was operating from Maqbool Alam Road in the Cantonment area. Despite being located close to the police officers’ residential colony, its activities had gone unnoticed. Acting on information provided by local residents, ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja led the raid with a police team, which exposed the illegal operation. Know about the entire matter in sequential order... Now know how it was exposed ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja said - Neighbors informed about running a sex racket in the house. The police team conducted a raid. As soon as the raid happened, Sameer Siddiqui fled from the spot. His wife Tarannum was caught by us. One boy and two girls were found in objectionable condition in one room. Then police started searching other rooms. Two rooms were locked. When police broke the locks, liquor bottles and objectionable items were found inside. Suspects are being interrogated According to police, currently the accused woman Tarannum and the arrested young man and woman are being interrogated. Their previous criminal records are also being investigated. ACP Cantt Nitin Taneja said- Police is constantly monitoring such activities. No one will be allowed to be above the law.

title: Chaos at Mayawati press conference after short circuit:Smoke fills hall, panic erupts; BSP supremo leaves without taking questions or cutting cake
summary: Chaos broke out during a press conference addressed by Mayawati on Wednesday when a short circuit occurred in a ceiling light at the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) office in Lucknow. Sparks were seen, and the hall quickly filled with smoke. Party workers present in the conference hall panicked as the situation unfolded. Security personnel immediately stepped in and used fire extinguishers to bring the situation under control. The press conference was called off soon after. Mayawati left the venue without cutting the cake and without taking questions from the media. Earlier, the BSP chief had made a strong statement on a recent meeting of BJP’s Brahmin legislators. She said the Brahmin community did not need “bati-chokha” from anyone but wanted respect. She added that if the BSP came to power, the aspirations of the Brahmin community would be fulfilled. She also cautioned Brahmins not to fall for the influence of the Congress, BJP or the Samajwadi Party. Speaking on the party’s electoral strategy, Mayawati made it clear that the BSP would contest all elections across the country on its own. She said the party would go solo in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections as well, and there should be no confusion on this issue. The remarks came in the backdrop of a meeting of BJP’s Brahmin MLAs held during the Assembly session. BJP’s state president Pankaj Chaudhary had expressed displeasure, calling the meeting a violation of party discipline. He had said he spoke to the MLAs individually and would take action. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had also taken a dig at the BJP. Referring to a New Year gathering, he remarked that BJP MLAs were sitting and eating litti-chokha, and questioned what would happen if they turned against the government. He sarcastically added that the BJP was now even investigating bati-chokha. Two key points from Mayawati’s press conference 1. Caste-based parties must change their mindset On alliances, Mayawati said a positive decision could be considered in the future only if caste-based parties abandoned casteist thinking and were able to transfer upper-caste votes to the BSP. However, she said this would take years, and until such a change happened, the BSP would not think of alliances. 2. No room for complacency in UP elections She alleged that the BJP, Congress and SP were using every possible tactic to weaken the BSP. A strong response was necessary, she said, and bringing the party to power in Uttar Pradesh was essential. She asserted that the people wanted the BSP in power and the party would leave no stone unturned in the upcoming elections. What was the meeting of Brahmin MLAs about? On December 23, a meeting of Brahmin MLAs was held in Lucknow during the winter session of the विधानसभा. The gathering, attended by BJP MLAs and some SP rebels, took place at the Lucknow residence of Kushinagar BJP MLA P. N. Pathak, officially on the occasion of his wife’s birthday. Around 45–50 Brahmin MLAs from Purvanchal and Bundelkhand attended the meeting, where litti-chokha and vrat food were served. After the meeting, political circles were abuzz. Sources said the Chief Minister’s OSD contacted Pathak, who maintained that it was only a community meal and not a political meeting. Senior RSS and BJP leaders were also said to be involved in defusing the situation. Why was the meeting held? Sources said the MLAs felt that while several castes had become powerful in caste-based politics, Brahmins were being sidelined. They alleged that Brahmin issues were being ignored and that despite having a deputy chief minister from the community, real power was lacking. The meeting was aimed at raising Brahmin concerns more assertively. Political analysts point out that although Brahmins constitute around 11–12 per cent of Uttar Pradesh’s population, they play a decisive role in nearly 30 districts. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP received about 89 per cent of Brahmin votes. The BSP had successfully used a Brahmin–Dalit social engineering formula in 2007 to come to power with a full majority under Mayawati. However, shifts in political alignment over the years saw Brahmin voters moving from the BSP to the SP in 2012 and later backing the BJP in 2017, when the party formed a full-majority government with significant Brahmin representation in the Assembly.

title: Devotees rush Ganga Ghats of Kashi on Makar Sankranti:Take holy dip, offer Khichdi to Baba Vishwanath, donate food, clothes and money; city police on alert
summary: A flood of devotion surged at the banks of Mother Ganga on Makar Sankranti festival on Thursday. Since early morning on Makar Sankranti, the atmosphere became devotional with chants of Har Har Gange, Namami Gange, Namami Mate. Devotees took holy dips in the Ganges, performed worship in temples, and earned spiritual merit by donating food, clothes, and money. By 10 AM, more than 3 lakh people had reached the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Ganga Ghats. Crowds were visible at various ghats of Kashi including Dashashwamedh Ghat, Sheetala Ghat, Panchganga Ghat, Assi Ghat, and up to Ganga Gotami Sangam Kaithi since morning, where people took holy baths and performed charitable acts. Meanwhile, the sequence of darshan and worship continues at Baba Darbar, and devotees also visited the Khichdi Baba Temple to receive the prasad of khichdi. See the pictures.... Police administration on alert on water and land For the safety of devotees coming to bathe in the Ganges on Makar Sankranti, 100 personnel on 25 boats are on alert. These include personnel from Water Police, NDRF, and PAC Flood Unit. Main ghats have been barricaded. Police from local stations are also deployed at the ghats. Police and administration are fully alert regarding the safety of devotees from the ghat to the Ganges. Importance of Makar Sankranti Pandit Vikas explained - Black gram (urad dal) has special significance on Makar Sankranti. That's why on this day khichdi is made by mixing black gram and rice, and it is offered to God. Along with this, donating khichdi is also beneficial. Besides khichdi, one must offer arghya to Sun God with black sesame seeds on this day. Along with this, donations of sesame seeds, jaggery, clothes, blankets etc. should also be made. Doing this brings the blessings of Sun God. It also brings happiness and prosperity in life. Entry through 5 gates at Kashi Vishwanath Temple After bathing at Baba Vishwanath's abode, people are arriving to offer khichdi while some are coming for darshan. The temple administration is allowing entry through 5 gates. The Chief Executive Officer said - our priority is that devotees should not have to stand in line for long, so adequate barricading has been done. Today the protocol is closed and touch darshan is also not being allowed. Performed aarti of Mother Ganga and Lord Surya on Makar Sankranti On the auspicious occasion of Makar Sankranti for nature conservation remembrance, Namami Gange performed aarti of the sun of Sanatan and Mother Ganga, the goddess of nature, while wishing for joy, harmony and environmental protection. Under the coordination of Rajesh Shukla, Namami Gange Kashi region coordinator and cleanliness brand ambassador of Municipal Corporation, the message of preservation of culture and nature was given through national flags and boards with cleanliness slogans.

title: ‘No place for non-believers in India, their place is Pakistan’:Satua Baba makes provocative statement at Magh Mela; denies owning any luxury possessions while seated in a Porsche
summary: “There is no place for non-believers in India. Their place is Pakistan. They should leave on time because the Rafale of development has already taken off here.” These remarks were made by Satua Baba, who often remains in the spotlight during the Magh Mela. Satua Baba has also drawn attention for his frequent use of luxury vehicles. On January 14, he reportedly stopped using his ₹3-crore Land Rover Defender and arrived in a Porsche 911 Turbo, said to be worth around ₹4.40 crore. Speaking to Bhaskar, Satua Baba said he has no attachment to luxury cars. “I don’t have any passion for these vehicles. I only know that if I sit in a car, it should take me to Kashi, Prayagraj or Ayodhya. That is all,” he said. He added that he does not know the names or prices of the cars he travels in and joked that “Google Baba” knows more about them. Q: You said there is no place for non-believers in India and that they should go to Pakistan. What did you mean? Satua Baba: Those who do not believe in India and Sanatan should understand that India is moving ahead. The Rafale of development has already taken off here. Those who do not connect with this thought will not find a place here. Q: You are often seen changing luxury vehicles. Recently, you arrived in a Porsche after using a Land Rover Defender. Why? Satua Baba: I do not have any passion for vehicles. I only know that a car should take me from one place to another. If I sit in a car in Kashi, it should take me to Prayagraj. If I leave from here, it should take me to Ayodhya. That is my only concern. Q: Do you know the price or features of these cars? Satua Baba: No. I do not know their names, features or prices. For that, there is Google Baba. I only know how to sit in a vehicle and reach my destination. Q: Many people question how a saint can travel in such expensive cars. What is your response? Satua Baba: Can spirituality not travel in these cars? Is Sanatan so weak that it will be misunderstood because of a vehicle? This is the speed of Sanatan. Those who tried to divide Sanatan and those who fired bullets at Ram will be crushed at this speed. Q: On Wednesday, you reached the Magh Mela in a Porsche. Was that intentional? Satua Baba: No. For me, a cart, a jeep, a Bullet, a JCB or a luxury car are the same. The goal is only to reach where I have to go and continue my work. Q: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said from the stage that people should connect with you. How do you see that statement? Satua Baba: It was not meant for me personally. It was for the ascetic form. Whoever connects with Sanatan connects with India. Q: You are seen meeting political and administrative figures at your ashram. Does that affect your spiritual role? Satua Baba: I meet everyone, but my main focus is on the Kalpavasis staying in the ashram. Serving devotees is my first duty. Q: What responsibility have you taken at the Magh Mela? Satua Baba: Satua Ashram is the largest ashram at the Magh Mela. Devotees keep coming with faith. It is the duty of a saint to give them shelter and support. We are doing that. Q: You praised the current government while speaking about development. What did you mean? Satua Baba: Those who did not give light to the poor, food to the hungry, or roads to the people are gone. This is Prime Minister Modi and Yogi’s India. Development will now move faster. Q: What message do you give to devotees coming to the Magh Mela? Satua Baba: Come with faith and devotion. Take a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam. Unite your family and society. India is now being discussed across the world. After 500 years, Ram reached Ayodhya, and the country is moving forward.

title: After losing to Indira, Raj Narain claimed vote theft evidence:How a fierce election dispute triggered disqualification, emergency rule reshaped India’s national politics forever
summary: From today begins The 'Rajneeti ki Rangbhoomi', a special series that chronicles the great political 'Mahabharata' of Uttar Pradesh, a battlefield where every move by leaders creates history. This series explores clashing ideologies, broken alliances, new friendships, dissolving factions and ever-shifting power equations. In the very first episode, we revisit one of the most dramatic political confrontations in Indian history, Raj Narain versus Indira Gandhi. Why did Raj Narain become a persistent thorn in Indira Gandhi’s path? How did this man eventually cause her disqualification, electoral defeat and the declaration of the Emergency? December 1970: A Political Earthquake in Delhi December 1970 was sending chills through Delhi’s power corridors. The political tension inside Rashtrapati Bhavan spilled out and scorched the entire nation. Suddenly, the news broke- 'The Lok Sabha has been dissolved. Elections will be held one year early.' The announcement exploded like a bomb in the opposition camp. In a smoke-filled secret room, senior opposition leaders gathered. One leader exhaled cigar smoke and remarked calmly,' Madam has played a masterstroke.' Another shot back sharply, 'If we fight alone, we will be chopped like vegetables.' 'So what’s the solution?' a third asked. After a brief silence, a single voice answered,' We fight together.' Congress splits: R Versus O The roots of this confrontation lay in 1969, when senior Congress leaders fell out with Indira Gandhi and expelled her from the party. Congress split into two factions. Indira’s faction was named Congress (R), R for Revolutionary. The old guard became Congress (O), O for Organisation. Both factions fought elections against each other. Congress (O)’s symbol was a woman spinning a charkha, while Congress (R) was allotted the cow and calf. As elections approached, Congress (O), Jan Sangh and the Socialists joined hands. The battle was no longer electoral, it was about proving who represented the 'real Congress'. Raebareli question: Indira stands firm On December 29, a packed press conference hall awaited Indira Gandhi. A journalist asked pointedly, 'Madam Prime Minister, is it true you may leave Raebareli and contest from Gurgaon?' The hall fell silent. Indira replied firmly. 'No.' 'Any particular reason?' the journalist pressed. 'I am not doing that. That is enough,' she said curtly. January 1971: The Search for a Challenger On January 19, opposition leaders met secretly again. One crucial question loomed, who would challenge Indira Gandhi in Raebareli? The answer echoed through the room: Raj Narain. One leader struck the table.'This man can keep power awake at night.' 'But will he agree?' someone asked. 'He fears no defeat,' came the reply. The contest was set, Raj Narain versus Indira Gandhi. This was no longer an election. It was war. Campaign sparks and sarcasm Indira Gandhi addressed a massive rally in Coimbatore. When Raj Narain’s name surfaced, a faint smile crossed her face. She declared sharply, 'The opposition has no face.' A voice from the crowd shouted,'And Raj Narain?' Indira retorted sarcastically, 'In Raebareli they have fielded someone who survives on criticism. He only knows how to shout against Nehruji.' Voting day and a crushing defeat Voting took place on March 7, 1971. Counting lasted days. Even before counting began, Raj Narain took out a victory procession on March 8, shouting,'This is democracy’s victory!' But on March 10, the tables turned. Congress (R) swept Raebareli. Indira Gandhi: 1,83,309 votes Raj Narain: 71,499 votes A margin of over 1.10 lakh. Raj Narain was stunned. 'This is impossible, those who marched with me, whom did they vote for?' The rumour of 'Magic Ink' Soon, whispers spread across Raebareli, of 'magic ink'. A supporter told Raj Narain,'This wasn’t voting, Netaji, it was chemistry.' 'What do you mean?' Raj Narain asked. 'They say the ink vanished, and the Congress symbol reappeared before counting.' 'If this is true,' Raj Narain replied grimly, 'I will drag this ink to court.' Taking the PM to Court In April 1971, Raj Narain approached Allahabad lawyer Ramesh Srivastava. 'I want to drag Indira to court,' he declared. 'You are challenging the Prime Minister,' the lawyer warned. 'There is no Prime Minister in law,' Raj Narain replied. 'Only a culprit.' Shanti Bhushan was brought in. He initially dismissed the 'magic ink' claim as absurd but later reframed it as mechanical fraud. A 258-page petition was drafted, listing eight serious charges, from misuse of government machinery to exceeding election expenditure limits. 'If even one is proven,' Shanti Bhushan warned, 'the Prime Minister will be in trouble.' June 12, 1975: The Verdict After four years of hearings, June 12, 1975 arrived. At 1 Safdarjung Road, PM’s residence, tension was unbearable. Teleprinters rattled. Inside Courtroom No. 24 of the Allahabad High Court, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha read the verdict calmly. Mrs Gandhi was found guilty of two corrupt practices, including using government officer Yashpal Kapoor in her campaign. At 10:20 am, UNI flashed the headline: 'Indira Gandhi Unseated.' Rajiv Gandhi informed his mother.'Mummy, they have disqualified you.' She replied quietly, 'So they finally did it.' Pressure, defiance and the Emergency Opposition leaders demanded resignation. Indira chose defiance. On June 25, JP’s rally at Ramlila Maidan thundered. Raj Narain declared,'Tomorrow we will gherao her residence.' That night, Emergency was imposed. Raj Narain was arrested at dawn. Opposition leaders were jailed. Parliament passed the 39th Amendment, barring courts from challenging the Prime Minister’s election. 1977: The Final Reckoning After 19 months, elections were announced. Raj Narain refused to contest from a 'safe seat'.'I will fight only from Raebareli,' he said. Campaigning fiercely, he attacked elitism and arrogant power. When the results were declared, history turned full circle. Raj Narain: 1,77,719 votes (52%) Indira Gandhi: 1,22,517 votes (35.7%) The man who once lost by over a lakh votes had returned to unseat the most powerful leader in the country. *** References The Case That Shook India: The Verdict That Led to the Emergency - Prashant Bhushan | Emergency Retold - Kuldip Nayar | Emergency Chronicles: Indira Gandhi and Democracy's Turning Point - Gyan Prakash | Raj Narain: Not Just a Name, History - Shahnawaz Ahmad Qadri | Raj Narain: The Path of Thought - Dhirendra Srivastava | State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain (Allahabad High Court Verdict) Individuals: Prof. Anand Kumar, Suresh Khairnar, Vijay Vidrohi, Dhirendra Srivastava, Shahnawaz Ahmad Qadri. title: Dimple Yadav simplicity stands apart in noisy Indian politics:Journey of daughter-in-law of UP's biggest political family reflects restraint, discipline and quiet influence
summary: While Indian politics is increasingly dominated by spectacle, luxury, and grand displays, there is one woman who remains far removed from this culture. She keeps herself away from controversies and excess, and her simplicity is often cited as exemplary, truly understated in every sense. She is Dimple Yadav, the wife of Akhilesh Yadav, the leading figure of Uttar Pradesh’s most prominent political family. Carrying forward the legacy of Mulayam Singh Yadav’s Lok Sabha seat, Mainpuri, she is currently serving her second term as MP from the constituency. She has also represented the Kannauj Lok Sabha seat twice. On her birthday today, her life and choices once again draw attention for all the right reasons. See 2 photos from her wedding- Simplicity in action Dimple Yadav is neither fond of jewellery nor display. An incident from March last year illustrates this clearly. While travelling from Mainpuri to Lucknow, she came across an accident involving two cars. Police and emergency help were delayed, and tensions were rising between the two parties involved. Dimple stepped out of her vehicle, calmed both sides, and ensured they were taken to hospitals. Notably, she arranged for them to be sent to different hospitals to prevent any further confrontation. It was a quiet intervention, without cameras or statements, characteristic of her approach to public life. Dimple stepped out of her vehicle, calmed both sides, and ensured they were taken to hospitals. Notably, she arranged for them to be sent to different hospitals to prevent any further confrontation. It was a quiet intervention, without cameras or statements, characteristic of her approach to public life. When a diamond necklace was returned Her indifference to jewellery is well known within political circles. In 2021, a leader visiting the Yadav residence brought an imported diamond necklace as a gift for Dimple. Akhilesh Yadav asked what the gift was and, upon seeing it, responded pointedly. 'Have you ever seen her wearing jewellery?' he asked. 'Do not spoil her habits. She has no interest in these things. Take it back.' The necklace was returned, reinforcing Dimple Yadav’s preference for simplicity over luxury. Staying away from controversies Dimple Yadav has consistently kept herself distant from political controversies. Even when faced with sensitive questions, her responses, or silence, reflect restraint. In July 2025, during a visit by the Imam of the Parliament mosque along with Samajwadi Party leaders, Dimple was also present. Some clerics questioned her presence, triggering a brief debate. Dimple chose not to respond publicly and stayed away from the controversy altogether, maintaining her long-held approach of not engaging in unnecessary disputes. Army upbringing Born in Pune in 1978, Dimple Yadav comes from a disciplined Indian Army family. Her father, Colonel Ram Chandra Singh Rawat, is a retired army officer, and her mother is Champa Rawat. Originally from Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district, her family’s postings meant she spent her childhood across Pune, Bathinda, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lucknow. She studied at Army Public School, Lucknow, and later graduated in Commerce from Lucknow University. The army environment instilled discipline, self-reliance, and simplicity. Horse riding has been a passion since childhood, and she trained regularly at the Lucknow Racecourse and Cavalry Club. Love story against odds Dimple and Akhilesh Yadav’s love story reads like a film script. They met at a friend’s house in Lucknow, and at the time, Dimple was unaware that Akhilesh was Mulayam Singh Yadav’s son. Friendship grew into love over four years, even enduring Akhilesh’s time studying in Australia. Initially, both families were opposed to the marriage, partly due to caste differences and political circumstances linked to the Uttarakhand movement. It was Akhilesh’s grandmother, Murti Devi, whose approval eventually brought acceptance. The couple married on 24 November 1999 in Lucknow, in a ceremony attended by figures such as Amitabh Bachchan and Rajesh Khanna. Politics, family, and public life After marriage, Dimple stayed away from politics for nearly a decade, focusing on her home and three children, daughters Aditi and Tina, and son Arjun. Gardening and family time remain her favourite pursuits. She entered electoral politics in 2009 from Firozabad but lost to Congress leader Raj Babbar. In 2012, following Akhilesh Yadav’s elevation as Chief Minister, she was elected unopposed from Kannauj in a by-election, becoming the first woman from Uttar Pradesh and the 44th person nationally to achieve this feat. She won again in 2014, lost in 2019, and returned strongly in 2022 from Mainpuri after Mulayam Singh Yadav’s death. She retained the seat in 2024. Even today, her understated presence in Parliament continues to draw attention, proof that simplicity still resonates in public life. title: Vulgar social media content sparks cyber complaint in Agra:Mother files FIR against content creator; influencer with lakhs of followers under probe
summary: A woman in Agra has lodged a complaint with the cyber police against a social media influencer after her children were allegedly exposed to obscene content while watching reels on her mobile phone. The woman said an inappropriate clip suddenly appeared on the screen, prompting her to immediately snatch the phone from the children. In her complaint, she named the Instagram user ID that was being watched, alleging that it regularly serves obscene videos. According to the complaint, some of the reels on the account have garnered up to 14 million views. The woman claimed that two Instagram accounts operate under the same name, each with around 4.5 lakh followers. The influencer is also said to have about 10,000 followers on Facebook. She alleged that several comments on the videos are highly objectionable and unfit for display, and that the reels feature explicit content with suggestive audio. Demanding swift action, the complainant urged the cyber police to take strict steps against the operator of the user ID to prevent children from being exposed to such content. See 2 pictures... Now read the full matter in detail… A woman in Agra has approached the cyber crime cell alleging that obscene content circulating on Instagram is having a harmful impact on children and society, after her own children were allegedly exposed to such material while watching reels on a mobile phone. The complainant, Ruby Tomar, a resident of Fatehabad Road under Tajganj police station limits, supplies Ayurvedic medicines. She said that on January 4, while visiting a beauty parlour in Kamla Nagar to deliver medicines, she noticed a woman watching reels on her phone when an obscene video suddenly appeared on Instagram. Shocked by the content, the woman immediately scrolled past the reel, remarking that such videos were having a dangerous effect on children and society. Ruby said a similar incident occurred the following day at her home. On January 5, her children were using Instagram while she was sitting nearby. After watching multiple reels for some time, the same influencer’s video allegedly appeared on the screen. She immediately took the phone away from the children and later visited the Instagram profile linked to the reel. According to her complaint, all the videos uploaded on the account contained obscene visuals, vulgar gestures and objectionable remarks about women, accompanied by suggestive audio. She alleged that such content promotes moral degradation and negatively influences young viewers. During her own inquiry, she claimed to have learnt that the woman creating the reels is a resident of Kamla Nagar in Agra. Ruby Tomar has since filed a formal complaint with the Agra cyber police station, demanding strict action. Police officials said efforts are under way to trace the Instagram ID, verify its operator and identify the woman behind the account.

title: ₹50-crore illegal toll collection exposed at UP toll plaza:Samajwadi Party leader, toll owner jailed; party alleges BJP MLA’s role in arrest
summary: A joint police–administration team in Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur district arrested four people, including a toll plaza owner, on January 9 for allegedly forcing tractor-trolleys to pay toll tax illegally. Superintendent of Police Sagar Jain said preliminary estimates suggest that nearly ₹50 crore was collected unlawfully in a single year. “We are scrutinising records of the past five years. The actual amount could be higher,” he said. The main accused, toll plaza owner Kamaljeet Pradhan, is associated with the Samajwadi Party and is seeking the party ticket from the Nakud assembly seat. Following his arrest, Samajwadi Party leaders have alleged political vendetta, claiming that the arrest was orchestrated to protect the political future of the sitting Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Mukesh Chowdhary. Police officials, however, denied any political pressure and said the action was taken after complaints that tractor-trolleys were being stopped and forced to pay toll despite being exempt under rules. To understand the case, Bhaskar visited the site, spoke to police officers to learn how the alleged fraud was carried out, and held separate conversations with leaders from both parties. This report presents the full ground reality and political claims surrounding the controversy. First understand the complete case Toll owner among four arrested, fake receipts recovered The Saharanpur district administration cracked down on illegal toll collection at the Sarsawa toll plaza after District Magistrate Manish Bansal received complaints that ₹130 was being forcibly collected from every tractor-trolley, despite rules clearly exempting such vehicles from toll on national highways. Acting on the complaint, the DM formed a special team, which conducted a raid on January 9. The allegations were found to be correct. Following the raid, toll plaza owner Kamaljeet Pradhan, toll manager Kalu Singh Ranawat, and toll workers Akshay Kumar and Sagar were arrested. The team recovered one receipt book, eight torn receipts and three handwritten slips containing details of toll collections. An FIR was registered at Sarsawa police station on the complaint of regional accountant Ramprasad Gupta. On January 12, the Saharanpur Civil Court rejected the bail pleas of all four accused. ₹130 collected from every tractor-trolley To understand how the alleged fraud was carried out, we spoke to Saharanpur SP (Rural) Sagar Jain. He said ₹130 was being collected from each tractor-trolley using fake receipts printed at the toll operator’s level. “Farmers were given these receipts after money was taken. During initial questioning, the toll owner admitted that this illegal collection had been going on for about one year,” SP Jain said. Police estimate that illegal toll collection worth nearly ₹50 crore may have taken place during this period. “We are examining toll records of the past five years. All documents are under scrutiny, and further involvement of other individuals cannot be ruled out,” the SP added. Why so many tractor-trolleys pass through this toll Experts say the toll plaza became a lucrative point because Saharanpur is a major hub of the wood-carving and furniture industry. Poplar cultivation is widespread in the district, with over 50,000 farmers engaged in poplar farming. Neighbouring Yamunanagar in Haryana, which borders Saharanpur, has more than 350 plywood factories. Most of the poplar produced in Saharanpur and nearby Dehradun is transported to these factories. Due to intense competition, plywood companies have set up direct purchase counters in farmers’ fields, from where wood is transported daily by tractor-trolleys. The Sarsawa toll plaza lies on the only direct route to Yamunanagar factories. The highway also connects Dehradun with Panchkula, and mining tractor-trolleys operating along the Yamuna belt use the same route. Over 13,000 vehicles pass daily During an on-ground visit, toll employees, speaking off camera, said around 13,000 vehicles passed through the plaza daily last year, and the number has increased further. After the police action, toll collection from tractor-trolleys has been stopped. Most tractor-trolley drivers declined to speak on camera, citing fear and routine daily travel through the route. Political allegations surface The arrests have triggered political controversy. Leaders of the Samajwadi Party have alleged that Kamaljeet Pradhan, who is seeking the party ticket from the Nakud assembly seat, was arrested due to political vendetta. SP leaders claim the action was taken to benefit the sitting Bharatiya Janata Party MLA from Nakud, Mukesh Chaudhary. Social media campaigns in support of Kamaljeet began soon after his arrest, with several SP leaders calling the case politically motivated. Former SP district president Farhad Gada said the family claims Kamaljeet had no role in toll operations and that he went to the police station on his own after receiving a call from the SHO. He alleged the family was not informed before Kamaljeet was sent to jail. Gada also questioned why the administration allowed alleged illegal collection for a year if it was aware of the practice. Claim linked to SIR controversy Farhad Gada further alleged that Kamaljeet was targeted after he raised objections on social media regarding changes in assistant appointments during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work in Saharanpur, claiming names from a particular community were removed. He alleged this angered those in power and led to Kamaljeet’s arrest. Former BJP MLA raises questions Former BJP MLA Shashibala Pundir also questioned the arrest in social media posts, alleging Kamaljeet was falsely implicated. She said she met him in jail and claimed he had no current financial dealings with the toll plaza. She has sought an impartial investigation from the district administration. BJP MLA denies allegations Responding to allegations, BJP MLA Mukesh Chaudhary said Kamaljeet is like his nephew and had worked with him during elections. “Why would I get him arrested?” he said, denying any role in the action. Chaudhary said multiple leaders, including ministers and MLAs, had spoken to officials after the arrest. “The government order clearly states that toll cannot be collected from anything attached to a tractor. It has been confirmed that toll was being collected illegally,” he said. Police maintain that the investigation is based strictly on evidence and documents recovered during the raid, and that political affiliations will not affect the probe.

title: Dense fog covers 30 districts of Uttar Pradesh:Temp drops to 3.1°C in Meerut; cars collide, over 50 trains delayed, weather likely to change soon
summary: Uttar Pradesh is grappling with severe cold as icy winds continue to intensify the chill. Night temperatures have plunged below Shimla (7.2 degrees Celsius) and Jammu (4 degrees Celsius), marking one of the coldest periods this season. Dense fog hits 30 districts Since Thursday morning, dense fog has enveloped 30 districts, including Agra, Bareilly, Ghaziabad, Gonda, Hathras, and Sambhal. In several areas, visibility has dropped below 10 meters, leaving roads deserted and creating hazardous travel conditions. Transportation disruptions The thick fog has disrupted both rail and air travel. More than 50 trains, including VIP services like Vande Bharat, have been delayed. Around 10 flights also took off late due to poor visibility. In Meerut, two cars collided late at night due to the fog, leaving one driver critically injured. First, look at two pictures Temperature records across the state Over the past 24 hours, every district in the state recorded temperatures below 10 degrees Celsius. Meerut emerged as the coldest city at 3.1 degrees Celsius, followed by Ayodhya at 3.5 degrees Celsius, Muzaffarnagar at 4 degrees Celsius, and Hardoi-Raebareli at 4.2 degrees Celsius. Previous day’s fog-related incidents On Wednesday, dense fog affected 25 districts, including Meerut, Sambhal, and Bulandshahr. Low visibility led to three accidents involving six vehicles, resulting in one death and injuries to 20 people, including 15 schoolchildren. Weather forecast Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh stated, “Western winds will continue to affect the state over the next 5–6 days, causing minimum temperatures in many districts to drop by 4–6 degrees Celsius. From January 19, isolated rainfall with drizzle is expected in parts of western Uttar Pradesh.”

title: 'You are insulting us by calling us Harijan,' shouts Mayawati:Moment that impressed Kanshi Ram, revealing unheard stories from ‘Behenji’s’ life on her 70th birthday
summary: It was a cold December night in 1977 in Delhi’s Inderpuri area. Around 11 pm, someone knocked at the door of a small, dilapidated house. When the homeowner, Prabhu Das, opened the door, he saw a middle-aged man wearing worn-out clothes and a muffler around his neck. The man introduced himself: “I am the president of BAMCEF. I have come to invite your daughter to deliver a speech in Pune.” That man was Kanshi Ram, and he was speaking about Mayawati, Prabhu Das’s sixth child. That single meeting changed Mayawati’s life forever. A young woman preparing to become an IAS officer would later go on to become Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh four times. Her supporters would lovingly call her ‘Behenji’. Today is Mayawati's 70th birthday. On this occasion, read some unique stories from her life in Dainik Bhaskar... The speech that caught Kanshi Ram’s attention A day before Kanshi Ram visited her home, 21-year-old Mayawati had delivered a fiery speech at Delhi’s Constitution Club. The then Health Minister Raj Narain repeatedly addressed Dalits as “Harijan” in his speech. When Mayawati came to the stage, she shouted angrily: You are insulting us by calling us ‘Harijan’. Her sharp words made headlines in Delhi newspapers the next day. After reading those reports, Kanshi Ram went looking for her. At that time, Mayawati’s house had no electricity. She was studying under the light of a lantern, preparing for the civil services. From IAS dream to mass leader In his biography Kanshi Ram: Leader of Dalits, Badri Narayan writes that Kanshi Ram asked Mayawati what she wanted to become. She replied that she wanted to be an IAS officer to serve her community. Kanshi Ram responded: What will you do by becoming an IAS officer? I can make you a leader before whom many collectors will stand in line. Mayawati immediately understood where her future lay. Her father strongly opposed her decision and asked her to stop meeting Kanshi Ram or leave the house. Mayawati chose the movement, left home, and began living in the party office. Hardship, courage and early struggles Before entering politics, Mayawati worked as a school teacher in Delhi. She used her savings, packed a few clothes in a suitcase, and left home—an extraordinary step for a young woman at that time. She often travelled long distances on a bicycle with Kanshi Ram to expand the Dalit movement. In 1984, together they laid the foundation of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). A brave childhood incident Born on 15 January 1956 in Delhi, Mayawati was known for her courage from a young age. When she was in Class 5, her newborn brother fell seriously ill. With no one else available, Mayawati carried him 7 km on her shoulders to a government hospital. Doctors were stunned by the child’s determination. The speech that made her a mass leader In 1986, Mayawati delivered a historic speech in Haridwar, questioning decades of Dalit political exploitation. Her powerful questions and direct answers electrified the crowd. The impact was immediate. In 1989, she won her first Lok Sabha election. BSP’s vote share exceeded that of the BJP. From setbacks to power Mayawati lost her first two elections but made a strong comeback in 1989. She later became a Rajya Sabha MP and the leader of BSP’s parliamentary party. In 1995, after withdrawing support from Mulayam Singh Yadav’s government, the infamous Lucknow Guest House incident took place, where she was attacked by Samajwadi Party workers. That very night, with BJP’s support, Mayawati was sworn in as Uttar Pradesh’s first Dalit woman Chief Minister. She went on to serve as CM four times, achieving a full majority in 2007 through her strategy of social engineering. Why Mayawati gave up wearing sarees and long hair After facing humiliation and caste-based taunts in Parliament, Mayawati became extremely strict about cleanliness and discipline. She stopped wearing sarees and cut her long hair short to save time during hectic schedules. No one is allowed to enter her room wearing shoes—a rule shaped by her early experiences of discrimination. The vote that brought down Vajpayee’s government In 1999, Mayawati played a decisive role in Indian politics when the BSP voted against the Vajpayee government, causing it to fall by just one vote—one of the most dramatic moments in parliamentary history. Allegations, decline and attempted comeback Between 2007 and 2012, Mayawati faced corruption allegations, including the Taj Corridor and NRHM cases. BSP’s political influence declined sharply after 2012. However, in 2025, Mayawati signalled a comeback by appointing her nephew Akash Anand as the party’s number-two leader and mobilising massive crowds on Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary, keeping hopes alive for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. From a lantern-lit room to the Chief Minister’s office, Mayawati’s journey remains one of defiance, discipline, and determination in Indian politics.

title: Ahilyabai Holkar statue damage sparks outrage from Kashi to Indore:Holkar Trust writes to Modi-Yogi to reinstall idols; administration say restoration work underway
summary: The demolition of a portion of the historic Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi for the redevelopment work has faced severe backlash. The Ghat, an integral part of Kashi’s spiritual landscape, was originally built in 1771 by Malwa’s revered ruler, Devi Ahilyabai Holkar. Allegations that this nearly 250-year-old heritage structure was damaged under a cremation Ghat development project have triggered strong emotional reactions, stretching from Uttar Pradesh’s Kashi to Madhya Pradesh’s Indore. The anger is particularly intense in Indore and across the Malwa region, where Ahilyabai Holkar is deeply revered. Considered not merely a regional queen but a pan-Indian symbol of cultural renaissance and public welfare, any harm to her legacy is being seen as far more than a routine construction dispute—it has become an issue of heritage, faith, and identity. The project: ₹18 crore development, but at what cost to heritage? According to administrative records, a cremation Ghat development project worth around Rs 18 crore is underway in the Manikarnika Ghat area. The project’s foundation stone was laid in 2023 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi. Officials say construction is being carried out over approximately 29,350 square meters. Given the marshy soil along the Ganga’s banks, piling work was done up to a depth of 15–20 meters to reach stable soil, ensuring structural safety during floods. Damage to Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy sparks controversy The controversy erupted when portions of the Ghat associated with Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy were allegedly damaged during construction. Eyewitnesses and local residents claim that old stone steps were demolished and several historical idols and religious symbols linked to Ahilyabai Holkar were damaged. Some idols were reportedly buried under debris, while others were found lying in the open. There are also reports of damage to a Shivling. The demolished section reportedly housed idols connected to Ahilyabai Holkar’s devotion to Lord Shiva. Allegations state that these artifacts were neither properly protected nor was prior permission taken from any historical authority or trust. Holkar trust alleges sudden demolition without notice The Manikarnika Ghat is overseen by the private Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Charities Trust. Its president, Yashwantrao Holkar, has strongly objected to the action. In a letter, he said, With deep sorrow and disappointment, we inform that the historic Manikarnika Ghat of Varanasi has been suddenly demolished in the name of development. In 1791, Punyashlok Devi Ahilyabai Holkar had renovated this site. It held immense spiritual significance for her. He alleged that on January 10, 2026, without any prior notice, officials of the Varanasi Municipal Corporation ordered the demolition, which was completed within hours—completely ignoring the site’s historical and cultural importance. “The goddess honoured in Kashi, now buried in rubble” Yashwantrao Holkar further pointed out the irony that Prime Minister Modi himself had installed a statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar in the Kashi Vishwanath temple complex, honoring her as a great protector of Indian culture. “Yet, the sacred and historic idols associated with the same Ahilyabai Holkar now lie buried in debris at Manikarnika Ghat,” he wrote. The Trust has announced that it is taking immediate steps to recover and reinstall the damaged idols and is also considering legal action against the responsible authorities. Demands placed before the PM and CM The Holkar Trust and members of the Holkar royal family of Indore have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, raising the following demands: Social organizations express anger Following the incident, outrage has grown among social organizations in Indore. Groups representing the Dhangar, Pal, and Baghel communities have announced a meeting on January 15 to decide their future course of action. They argue that such treatment of Ahilyabai Holkar’s legacy is unacceptable, especially when the nation has just concluded celebrations marking her 300th birth anniversary. Historians call it an attack on national heritage Senior historian Zafar Ansari termed the incident deeply distressing. “Devi Ahilyabai is not just the pride of Malwa or Maheshwar; she is a heritage figure for the entire nation. Every one of her works reflected foresight and public welfare,” he said. Ansari recalled that on May 31, 2025, the country celebrated Ahilyabai Holkar’s 300th birth anniversary. Prime Minister Modi visited Madhya Pradesh during the commemorations, inaugurated development projects in Bhopal, and released a commemorative postage stamp and a Rs 300 silver coin in her honor. Restoration funded by private royal property Historians also note that the temples and ghats built or restored by Ahilyabai Holkar were funded from her Khasgi (private royal property), not from the state treasury. The Holkar state maintained a distinct khasgi system, considered the queen’s personal wealth, through which hundreds of temples across India were built and preserved. Legal questions raised Experts point out that construction at a site like Manikarnika Ghat requires special caution under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. Strict regulations govern construction around historic and heritage sites. As a result, the issue has now moved beyond religious sentiment and public emotion, raising serious questions about administrative accountability and possible legal violations. About Manikarnika Ghat Manikarnika Ghat holds a unique place among Kashi’s 84 major ghats. According to legend, a jewel (Karnika) from Goddess Parvati fell here, giving the ghat its name. It is believed that cremation at this site grants liberation (Moksha). Devi Ahilyabai Holkar developed the ghat extensively, building Dharamshalas, temples, food centers, and bathing facilities for pilgrims. The ghat also shares a deep spiritual connection with the Kashi Vishwanath Dham. As the debate intensifies, authorities in Varanasi have stated that restoration work is underway. However, for many across Malwa and beyond, the incident has already struck a raw nerve—turning a development project into a national conversation on heritage, faith, and respect for history.

Previously holding the additional charge, Aggarwal, a 1994-batch officer, will now lead the premier counter-terrorism probe body until his superannuation in August 2028. This appointment solidifies his leadership of the agency's crucial national security mandate.

title: Today's youth is no longer just a 'job seeker', but a 'job creator': Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
summary: The programme is being organised by the Directorate of Training and Technical Education (DTTE) of the Government of Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Minister of State and the Chief Minister interacted with young innovators, teachers, investors and startup founders from universities, colleges and technical institutions, and reviewed the exhibition of student-led innovations.

Hyderabad: NCB seizes 813 kilograms of ganja and arrests three in crackdown
summary: Hyderabad NCB busted a major interstate ganja racket, seizing 813 kg of contraband and arresting three individuals on January 13, 2026. The specially modified lorry, carrying drugs from Odisha to Maharashtra, was intercepted near Hyderabad. Investigators uncovered a hidden compartment used for smuggling, with one accused having a prior narcotics record. The probe aims to dismantle the entire syndicate.

Shaksgam Valley: India bristles over China's fresh claim - dispute explained
summary: China's renewed claim over the Shaksgam Valley, an area India considers its integral territory, has reignited a strategic dispute. Beijing's defense of infrastructure construction, linked to CPEC, draws a sharp response from New Delhi, which rejects the 1963 China-Pakistan boundary agreement as illegal and invalid.

title: ‘Keeping a close watch’: Army chief says Operation Sindoor still ongoing; forces monitoring every enemy move
summary: Operation Sindoor, a swift 22-minute joint military strike on nine terror camps in Pakistan, remains active, with India maintaining vigilant surveillance. Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi highlighted this decisive response to the Pahalgam attack, showcasing India's readiness to protect national interests and sovereignty. The operation also saw veterans contributing to strategic planning.

title: President Murmu receives credentials from US, Austrian and Trinidad & Tobago envoys at Rashtrapati Bhavan
summary: President Droupadi Murmu received credentials from the new ambassadors of the United States and Austria, and the High Commissioner of Trinidad and Tobago at Rashtrapati Bhavan. US Ambassador Sergio Gor highlighted the strong relationship between the US and India, emphasizing dialogue to resolve differences. Austrian Ambassador Dr. Robert Zischg expressed his honor and looked forward to deepening bilateral engagement.

From Chabahar to Kashmir: Why chaos in Iran hurts India, benefits China & Pakistan
summary: India watches Iran's protests with unease, fearing a weakened state would disrupt its strategic environment. Iran serves as India's vital western corridor to Central Asia via Chabahar Port and a crucial counterweight to Pakistan's regional influence. A collapse risks jeopardizing connectivity projects and India's multi-alignment policy.

title: Umar Khalid and the UAPA question: Why bail remains elusive — Decoding Supreme Court ruling
summary: The Supreme Court denied bail to student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots case, citing a "hierarchy of culpability." While five co-accused were granted bail, the court found Khalid and Imam to be "ideological drivers" central to the alleged conspiracy's planning and preparation, distinguishing their roles from mere facilitators.

Aravali degradation: Encroachments, mining and urban sprawl hit ecology; study flags threat to groundwater, biodiversity
summary: A new study reveals that encroachments, deforestation, and urban expansion have severely damaged the Aravalli ranges, impacting groundwater, biodiversity, and air quality. The report highlights the weakening of the Aravalli's role as a green barrier, accelerating desertification and threatening ecological stability in northern India. A community-inclusive eco-restoration model is proposed to address these critical issues.

title: 'Leave Iran': India's stark advisory amid threat of US attack; protests spread
summary: India has issued an advisory urging its citizens in Iran to depart immediately due to escalating regional tensions and internal protests. The advisory, released by the Indian embassy in Tehran, advises students, pilgrims, business persons, and tourists to leave by available transport, including commercial flights, amid concerns of potential US military action and reported fatalities from unrest.

title: India–Greece ties: First-ever joint services staff talks held in Delhi; defence cooperation set to deepen
summary: India and Greece have initiated their first Joint Services Staff Talks in New Delhi, aiming to bolster defence partnerships and military-to-military cooperation. The dialogue focused on expanding bilateral engagement through exchange programs, capability development, and enhancing operational ties, signaling a new era of trust and shared security commitments.
